name: Filthoid Carapace
desc: Keratin grown from the skin of Filthoids, forming their hardest armor. Processed with special techniques, it can be used for protection in weapons and armor.
desc2:
"Those Filthoids have shells as tough as iron! You'd need a blade sharper and harder than steel to hunt 'em down."

— Lunosmith

name: Damaged Sal Volatile
desc: A shattered Sal Volatile bottle with deep scratches and bullet holes. Its contents leaked out but the glass bottle can be recycled.
desc2:
"The rain was relentless, pelting down. I rummaged through my pockets, holding up glass jar after jar to her nose, but she never again woke up to stroke my head with a smile. I know she's gone to a far, far better place than here."

— Fina, Citizen of Icelake

name: Cleansing Water
desc: Cleansing Water used by the Elysian Church devotees to cleanse their hands before ceremonies, usually kept in blessed containers inside temples.
desc2:
"In time's flowing river, we meet and part, enfolded in 'Her' embrace to the journey's end, returning to life's very heart."

— Tal, Unofficial Preacher of Elysian Church

name: Legion Nameplate
desc: Carried by Hyperborean soldiers, engraved with their name, rank, legion, and enlistment date. If a soldier falls in battle, their legion uses the name plate to identify them, and it is sent back to their hometown as a mark of honour.
desc2:
"To some soldiers, a medal of honour holds more weight than life itself. Too bad that I'm not cut from that noble cloth."

— Randy, Hyperborean Officer

name: Stone Powder
desc: Natural stone powder, commonly used as a consumable in alchemy and construction. The type of ore varies in colour due to geographical differences, making it a primary material for paint pigments.
desc2:
"Blinded, the stones began to whisper to me... their murmurs guiding my chisel, crafting shapes they yearned to become."

— Vina, Elysian Sculptor

name: Auspicious Scroll
desc: Parchment scrolls carried by Elysian knights, inscribed with blessings and prayers. Knights draw strength from these blessings in battle.
desc2:
"The Holy Iris Knights, Elysium's devout defenders, clad in shining armours, battling for thy faith. In this grand crusade, blessed by His hand, with Him at thy side, invincible thou shalt stand."

— Eilon, 132nd Commander of the Holy Iris Knights, "Pre-Battle Speech"

name: Signal Cable
desc:
A roll of cable with a Hyperborean mark, collected in a somewhat brutal way. 
Be careful of electric shocks before the sparks die out.
desc2:
"Hey, kid, fancy a firework show? Follow this genius's lead — spark up that wire, and I promise, you'll see the grandest fireworks ever!"

— Oliver the Bomb Expert

name: Repulsive Crystal
desc: Solid crystals harvested from rare Filthoids. Commonly used for intricate research into the biology of these enigmatic creatures.
desc2:
"Humanity's tale is one of combat with Filthoids. For fifteen centuries, we've but 'driven them away', never truly vanquished them... for true understanding had always eluded us... Now, the tide turns. The Repulsive Crystal's unveiling, I believe, marks our first stride towards a true 'triumph' over them."

— Timbergen, Pioneer of Filthology at Spathatoi, in "History of Filthoids: From the High Tower to the Mosken Sea"

name: Vermilion Teardrop
desc:
Common wild plants. The flowers are usually muti-petaled, bright red, and glossy. They are hardy, drought-resistant, and adaptable, hence widespread across the continent. 
They are said to be the tears Father Ask shed for the deceased Mother Embla during his journey to find her in Charon's mythology.
desc2:
"Through wilderness, thorns pierce his bare feet;
Still, his haste unceased.
In search for the lost beloved,
Until his arms, aloft, turn to towering peaks,
His blood and tears bloom into crimson wreaths."

— Lirico, Wandering Bard, in "Tales of the Misty Sea"

name: Creeping Tendrils
desc:
A creeping plant commonly found in shaded areas, highly flexible with intertwined fibers. After processing, they are used in various applications, and they are durable and resistant to wear. 
Said to be the inspiration for cable design.
desc2:
"Also known as the Ashless Wood, dark in colour, with leaves white as bone; resembling rotten timber, yet flame shuns its touch.
Its bark is edible, with an astringent and cold taste, non-toxic.
Can soothe swollen throats and quell inner heat, taken twice daily in a brew."

— Fufeng, Huaxu Apothecary, in "Essentials of Medicinal Herbs"

name: Filthoid Clot
desc: A thick grease extracted from Filthoids. Its viscosity often correlates with the Filthoid's strength.
desc2:
"How come the villains in stories never cry? Is it because their tears are too thick, like jelly? Or is it because their hearts are so cold that their tears are frozen for eternity?"

— Fina, Citizen of Icelake

name: Chain
desc: Produced from the Elysian Church. Their knight's standard attire has a fine chainmail made of numerous delicate chains. The clanking of the chainmail is the best declaration of battle as the knights march.
desc2:
"The Elysian Church seemed ready for war, with legions of knights silently invoking the divine name, marching towards the borders in shimmering silver chainmail and golden helms. As they gathered, the vast plains glittered like a lake of gold and silver. Many swore, in that day's sunlight, they glimpsed the divine shadow leading Elysium to triumph."

— Tacitus, Elysian Historian, in "Chronicles"

name: Luno Memento
desc: A currency unique to the Lunos, often given as a thank-you gift by those seeking help.
desc2:
"Luno Coins are really valuable! And these are a token of our friendship, so you better take good care of them!"

— Snow the "Demon King"

name: Snowswift Tail Feather
desc: Snowswift is a bird native to cold regions, commonly seen around Icelake. Known for their blistering speed in flight, these elusive creatures are rarely spotted by the naked eye, except during snowfalls when they perch quietly on branches or nestle in their nests. Historically, their tough feathers were prized for crafting traditional quills. Today, however, only a handful of traditionalists and those less fortunate continue to use these economical, albeit less durable, feather pens.
desc2:
"When the spring breeze sweeps across the snowy plains and brushes through the branches, the birds adorn themselves with airy new feathers, leaving their old winter plumage behind for those who pour their thoughts onto paper... It is with these less delicate feathers that Fina's dreams soar high."
 
 — Fina, a resident of Icelake

name: Metallic Armour
desc: A replaceable metal armor from the Hyperborean Empire on soldiers' standard uniforms, usually fitted at joints, with excellent shock resistance, and has been mass-produced. Two spare armors are now standard for a Hyperborean assault soldier.
desc2:
"Heavy they might be, they must be carried at all times. More than a mere legion order, it's a safeguard. I wish for you all to return home unscathed."

— Rhythm, Soldier of Icelake Escort

name: Blessing Trinketry
desc: Produced from the Elysian Church, a shield-shaped ornament worn by the Elysian Church soldiers. It's believed to be imbued with divine blessings, symbolizing the will to protect the church.
desc2:
"O Lord of Life and Bounty! May Your boon be everlasting upon me, let Elysium always bask in Your guardianship, our pure hearts forever in Your embrace."

— The Elysian Church Prayer

name: Vehicle Armour
desc: Produced from Hyperborea. Ensuring the legion's mobility has always been a key subject to the Aeolipile. Vehicle armor, serving as an external accessory, withstands extreme weather and allows the vehicle to hold up longer under gunfire. It can be quickly removed for full-speed advance.
desc2:
"The blizzards of the north are devastating to both soul and shoddy homes. Winter's toll ran high until the Aeolipile devised 'iron rooftops'. Merely crude, hefty iron plates, yet they averted snow's deadly weight — from that year on, there were almost no deaths from snow. This technique was later adapted for military use; though, rumour has it, the military still hasn't paid them for the patent."

— Dylan the Walking Encyclopedia, in "Into the Unseen Corners"

name: Statue Debris
desc:
The Statue of the Goddess of Fate built by the Elysian Church, now too damaged to discern its original form, but still exuding elegance among its ruins. 
Over time, new sprouts grow here. Under the decoration of vitality, myths never seem to fade.
desc2:
"Thy spring of youth hath waned, ne'er to renew."

"Yet, 'tis not a cause to sheathe the blade."

"Thy light of wisdom hath dimmed, ne'er to relume."

"Yet, 'tis not a cause to mute the words."

"Thy path to return doth end, ne'er to tread anew."

"Yet, 'tis not a cause to halt the advance."

"O valiant soul bereft of might, mind, and home! The hero with nothing left to offer for war! Heed Destiny's inquiry — what dost thy heart yearn? Whither dost thy blade drive?"

— Anonymous Poet, Excerpt from "The Spindle of the Goddess of Fate"

name: Fuel Reagent
desc: A concentrated combustion aid developed by the Alchemy Academy. A pungent, colourless liquid dyed red to denote danger. Used only in military or industrial settings. A few spoonfuls can send a fireplace's flames roaring up the chimney, and that's definitely an unwanted spectacle.
desc2:
"It burns fiercer than the most dangerous flame of love!"

— Rebecca, Perfumer of Luca

name: Insulation Coating
desc: A common industrial material. A viscous white latex-like liquid that maintains a balance in temperature. Given the unpredictability of terrain and climate on adventures, carrying a few cans is wise. The manufacturer recently introduced fruit and floral scents, so consumers are hereby warned to beware of accidental ingestion.
desc2:
"No, Filbert! I know they smell good, but they'll give you ouchies in your tummy! Come on, let's go find some yummy berries and mushrooms for you, okay?"

— Truffle, Commissary of Elysium

name: Sacred Candle
desc: Candles used in church ceremonies, accompanied by devoutly crafted candlesticks. Though their burn time is brief, their light suffices to illuminate the face of divine.
desc2:
"Under the argent moon's glow, we kneel to light the sacred candles,
Hailing the Weaver of Fate's thread.
May the sacred flame never be extinguished,
As its radiance endures eternal."

— The Elysian Church Prayer

name: Fluid Alloy
desc:
One of the alchemical products of the Hyperborean Empire. A liquid metal that seems like it could flow through your fingers at any moment. Made using a complex purification process. It's usually employed in the military industry.
If you can't handle their melting point, it is recommended not to heat them recklessly.
desc2:
"It reminds me of the flow of time... Like time, it heals fractures, veils the past, feigns that all is well. Indeed, its true intent was to reinforce crumbling old structures. But everything has its limits; under intense heat, it violently explodes, erasing all, be it old or new."

— Emerald, Aeolipile Material Scientist, in "Principles and Instructions for Use of New Materials"

name: Gold Sand
desc: A special product from the other side of the desert. It can be crafted into exquisite decorations or used to strengthen components. The final quality depends on how much real sand gets mixed in during transportation—since it is hard to distinguish between the two, deal with trusted merchants if necessary.
desc2:
"Here I lay in eternal repose,
Beneath countless sand grains,
With no opulent sepulchre,
But at dawn's light,
My golden grave gleams bright."

— "The Gold Miners' Evening Bell", a Khemet ballad

name: Filthoid Tentacle
desc:
A tentacle obtained from Filthoids, must be cleaned of mucus before use. They are very tough and have strong adhesive properties, sometimes used as fixation devices. 

These walking materials are everywhere, but not many can make them lie still on the chopping board.
desc2:
"Don't cut it in front of me! I can't watch this... aaaaaaaargh!"

— Demon Tabethe the Red Hand

name: Propulsion Unit
desc: A precision instrument made by the Hyperborean Empire, still intact despite being covered in scratches and pry marks.
desc2:
"Some boxes are to be opened, others not — thought that was common sense. If it's a holiday gift from Mom, go ahead, rip it open; but if it's a box made of fine iron, glowing eerily from the inside, with a big warning sign saying DANGER on it, you'd better chuck it into a ditch right away. But no one listened to me, so now I'm the only one left sitting here. *sigh*"

— Testimony taken after an accident

name: Contact Index
desc:
A book with intricate decorations, appears to be a valuable collection of poems, but is actually a codebook for deciphering internal legion radio communications. 
Unfortunately, the inner pages are damaged, leaving only some irrelevant secret codes that can't really be used to decrypt telegrams.
desc2:
Once you've familiarised yourself with the info, you might get rid of the used pages and repurpose the rest as a regular notebook.

" 12 05 01 22 05 20 08 05 02 01 19 05
04 05 19 20 18 15 25 20 08 05 06 09 12 05 19
01 14 04 05 22 01 03 21 01 20 05 14 15 23"

— A piece of simple code left on a notebook

name: Sharpening Potion
desc: Produced from the Elysian Church, a honey-like oily liquid that increases the sharpness of cold weapons and also maintains firearms. Almost every soldier of the assembly carries a few bottles with them, and during breaks, they can be seen carefully applying the potion to their weapons and silently reciting prayers for repelling enemies.
desc2:
"Beside me descends the scythe-bearing deity,
Forbidding retreat, hesitation, or doubt.
I shall be the extension of its blade,
I shall be the embodiment of its will, 
I shall slay without mercy,
Till all foes rest under its wings named Death."

— Extracted from the Elysian Scriptures, "Hymnal Vol. 2"

name: Projectile
desc: Produced from the Hyperborean Empire, a type of modified bullet that can explode. Equipped with a variety of interchangeable heads for different functional needs, experts can use different bullet characteristics to explode exactly where they want.
desc2:
"Its design was inspired by hunting — my family used to be hunters, and we had to cater to various needs of clients. If the prey's size was all that mattered, sheer firepower could do the trick; for fur preservation, the bullet's impact had to be internal, minimising external damage; as for pets, the wounds needed to be treatable — a real challenge! At first, I just wanted to make Dad's life easier, with no plan to create anything big. Sadly, these bullets ended up on the battlefield, and not even a shell found its way back to him."

— Nisaea, Aeolipile Master Gunsmith, in casual conversation at a secret tea party, recorded in "Gatherings Under the Night-Blooming Jasmine"

name: Weaponholder
desc: A widely used auxiliary bracket equipped with various clasps for a stable structure, allowing craftsmen to fix weapons on it for adjustment.
desc2:
"Few know that the Gad Weaponholder was the first patented invention. When the patent system was first introduced, no one was willing to risk their trade secrets; while the Gad Weaponholder is simple in technology, so it was put forward to test the waters. Of course, it ended up being a tremendous success. Ol' Gad could have made a fortune from this patent, but, 'I've made a mere holder ace all my life. I'm just glad you all like it. Go ahead, use it as you wish, for free!' said he. Quite touching, isn't it?"

— Dylan the Walking Encyclopedia, in "Into the Unseen Corners"

name: Serum Syringe
desc: A specialized spraying device for equipment, used to uniformly apply rust-proofing agents to extend the durability of equipment, and increase the performance of some weapons. Mixing it up with serum injectors can have severe consequences, so it must be used with caution.
desc2:
"Even among us nerds, she's the weird one. I thought the comment about us holding research as dear as life was only metaphorical, yet to her, it was for real. Why do you think she'd put rust inhibitor in a syringe? Because 'the apparatuses are living things, and the rust inhibitor is their serum; what else would I use for injection but a syringe?' I mean, wow..."

— Anonymous Alchemist, in casual conversation at a secret tea party, recorded in "Gatherings Under the Night-Blooming Jasmine"

name: Filthoid Polymer
desc: A polymer made from the concentrated tissues of Filthoids, resembling a tumor and surrounded by some tentacles, supposedly. The methods of producing and using Filthoid polymers apparently originated from the Spathatoi.
desc2:
"When humans suffer heavy blows, muscles and fat provide cushioning. Similarly, if materials react too violently to the point of mutual annihilation, structures similar to Filthoid tissues can slow down the process; I suppose this is a way of recycling. Perhaps we should erect a monument for these creatures who sacrificed themselves for the alchemical cause."

— Ecodna, Chief of Biological Applications at The Spathatoi, in "Disassembly and Reassembly: Biology of Filthoids"

name: Coolant
desc: A cold liquid collected from the north, stored in special containers. Even at room temperature, ice crystals form on the surface of the container. This notion, often found in poetry, is now used as a coolant.
desc2:
"Take me to see the glacial blues of the North,
Beneath the grey canopy of sky,
Where a vast ocean of stern, metallic hues lies."

— Lirico, the Wandering Bard, in "Tales of the Misty Sea"

name: Chest Key
desc: A little key that someone left behind. It can be used to open a locked chest.

name: Brunetto's Storage Box Key
desc: A little key that someone left behind. It can be used to open a locked chest.

name: Lost Silver Coin
desc: A silver coin without owner. It's hard to find its owner.

name: Gravel Ore
desc: Though not precious in the eyes of the refining market, these clear and sparkling ores hold the heart's true value, which can become the first piece of jewelry given to a beloved one.

name: Ancient Shield
desc: An old shield. It was discarded for no reason.

name: Hostless Medal
desc: A long lost medal. Its former owner once used it to exchange current coins.

name: Empty Bottle
desc: When it comes to waste items, the first things that always come to mind are empty bottles and cans. Collecting a small amount and selling them can help people maintain basic food and clothing, but that's all it can do.

name: Withered Branch
desc: It can be used to make simple tools or for heating, the most basic things for survival in the wilderness.

name: Goddess Gem
desc: A gemstone that has rested on the hand of a goddess statue on Purgatorio Island for a very long time. If it could speak, it would surely have many stories to tell, but it is, in fact, just a radiant and splendid gem.

name: Purgatorio Island: Volume Ⅰ
desc: A collection of enigmatic pages discovered by chance. Some are delicate scrolls of fine parchment; others, freshly printed sheets with ink still crisp and dark. A few are no more than torn scraps from half-used notebooks. Whether neatly penned or barely legible, they all share one thing in common — each contains a hint pointing to the whereabouts of a hidden treasure.
desc2:
January 1st
Today, ▇▇▇▇ gave me some Phoxene shards as "pocket money." She said that back in the capital, kids get pocket money from their elders before they come of age — to spend on treats or toys.
There aren't any shops around here, so she told me to save it. Then, when there's something I really want or need, I can use it to ask for her help.
Thing is... I can't really think of anything I want.


January 2nd
I've got it! I could get {nickname} a "birthday present"! Maybe one of those "birthday cakes" kids in the capital have when they turn a year older — I read they're really tasty! They might be expensive... but if I save enough pocket money to give to ▇▇▇▇, I bet she could help me get one.
I found an old clay jar in the kitchen. It's just right for keeping my savings.


January 16th
We were playing hide-and-seek today, and {nickname} found the jar and almost opened it... I need to find a better hiding spot.
Maybe tomorrow I'll sneak into the room where ▇▇▇▇ does her alchemy work. There are loads of strange machines in there — she never lets {nickname} go near them.


January 17th
I hid my piggy bank under the <H>waterfall, right next to the alchemy chamber</>. That way, neither {nickname} nor ▇▇▇▇ will stumble across it.


...


▇▇ ▇▇
{nickname}'s birthday is coming up, and I've saved a whole box full of pocket money. It should be enough for a cake. But ▇▇▇▇ seems really busy these days. She's been staying up late a lot... Maybe it's not the right time to bother her. I guess I'll ask her next year.
With another year of saving, I can get an even bigger cake — big enough for all three of us.

name: Purgatorio Island: Volume Ⅱ
desc: A collection of enigmatic pages discovered by chance. Some are delicate scrolls of fine parchment; others, freshly printed sheets with ink still crisp and dark. A few are no more than torn scraps from half-used notebooks. Whether neatly penned or barely legible, they all share one thing in common — each contains a hint pointing to the whereabouts of a hidden treasure.
desc2:
Dear Berry,
 
 If you are reading this letter, it means you've returned after all.
 You've always been a good girl, and I trust you had your reasons for coming back.
 I've left some supplies for you, buried <H>near the airship</> — they should be enough to get you both off Purgatorio Island.
 I wish you the best on your journey. Stay safe.

name: Purgatorio Island: Volume Ⅲ
desc: A collection of enigmatic pages discovered by chance. Some are delicate scrolls of fine parchment; others, freshly printed sheets with ink still crisp and dark. A few are no more than torn scraps from half-used notebooks. Whether neatly penned or barely legible, they all share one thing in common — each contains a hint pointing to the whereabouts of a hidden treasure.
desc2:
The Goddess of Fate weaves the stars into their paths, gifting us with guiding lights that lead us towards eternal bliss.
 Yet, in our times, humanity has strayed from Her teachings. We have forsaken the bonds of love and compassion, choosing instead to arm ourselves with cold steel against our own kin. Our sacred lands have crumbled, and even Her sanctuaries have been defiled.
 Should this be the ordeal She has devised — a sombre prelude to the dawn — then to you, the destined one who will one day reach this place, I offer a blessing that transcends time.
 
 In <H>a place overlooked by Her gaze</>, I have hidden the final legacy of an age when humanity cherished love and solidarity.
 May Her tender threads of fate lead you to the true dawn.

name: Purgatorio Island: Volume Ⅳ
desc: A collection of enigmatic pages discovered by chance. Some are delicate scrolls of fine parchment; others, freshly printed sheets with ink still crisp and dark. A few are no more than torn scraps from half-used notebooks. Whether neatly penned or barely legible, they all share one thing in common — each contains a hint pointing to the whereabouts of a hidden treasure.
desc2:
Time, slips swiftly by, ever a fading treasure.
In the distant corners of memory, truth stays hidden.
Having pierced countless illusions, the path leads under.
Through winding stone, with divine light, to the forgotten cave.
In lands devoid of life and hope, a new cycle takes root.

name: Icelake: Volume Ⅰ
desc: A collection of enigmatic pages discovered by chance. Some are delicate scrolls of fine parchment; others, freshly printed sheets with ink still crisp and dark. A few are no more than torn scraps from half-used notebooks. Whether neatly penned or barely legible, they all share one thing in common — each contains a hint pointing to the whereabouts of a hidden treasure.
desc2:
Sorry, babe, there's been a hiccup at home, so I can't take you to the inner city this month as I promised. But hang tight, I'll come for you as soon as I sort things out. Trust me one more time, okay?
 As a little something to make it up to you, I've hidden some cash <H>under the grass on the left side of the pathway</> to the inner city. Don't forget to pick it up. Love you!
 
 <W>You liar! You jerk! Every time you lie to me, you just throw money at me like I'm some kind of pet you own! I'd rather starve or drop dead in the street than take another coin from you! You can rot with your filthy money for all I care!</>

name: Icelake: Volume Ⅱ
desc: A collection of enigmatic pages discovered by chance. Some are delicate scrolls of fine parchment; others, freshly printed sheets with ink still crisp and dark. A few are no more than torn scraps from half-used notebooks. Whether neatly penned or barely legible, they all share one thing in common — each contains a hint pointing to the whereabouts of a hidden treasure.
desc2:
Hey there! Are you tired of struggling to make ends meet?
Sick of breaking your back every day for a pittance, only to be treated like dirt?
Do you feel like, no matter how hard you try, you just can't catch a break?
Don't beat yourself up — it's not your fault. What you're lacking isn't skill, but a stroke of luck! All you need is the right opportunity, and you could be the next bigshot!
And guess what? It's your lucky day! Just last month, the chief engineer of our Legendary Mining Alliance unveiled a new mining marvel, ten years in the making! It is user-friendly, boasts an impressive battery life, and the cherry on top — it can automatically extract microscopic Phoxene particles — invisible to the naked eye — and turn them into solid Phoxene! With this revolutionary technology, we can breathe new life into the exhausted mines and bring Icelake's mining industry back from the brink!
 
We're on the lookout for partners right now! Opportunities like this come once in a lifetime!
Want in? Solve the puzzle below for a chance to join our elite team!
 
(Beneath the text is a simple map of the slums with a Phoxene symbol marking a spot — it appears to be near <H>a pile of old junk by the roadside rubbish bin</>.)

name: Icelake Ⅲ
desc: A collection of enigmatic pages discovered by chance. Some are delicate scrolls of fine parchment; others, freshly printed sheets with ink still crisp and dark. A few are no more than torn scraps from half-used notebooks. Whether neatly penned or barely legible, they all share one thing in common — each contains a hint pointing to the whereabouts of a hidden treasure.
desc2:
Someone found my secret stash last time...
This time, I consulted a professional, who suggested I hide it somewhere outside the city, perhaps <H>somewhere near a puddle</>.
Sure, Phoxene won't go bad in water, but what if the box gets mouldy or rots from the moisture? Then my stash would literally be "money down the drain", right?
Still, it's better than having it stolen... I'm going to give it a shot. I'll check on it next week.

name: Icelake Ⅳ
desc: A collection of enigmatic pages discovered by chance. Some are delicate scrolls of fine parchment; others, freshly printed sheets with ink still crisp and dark. A few are no more than torn scraps from half-used notebooks. Whether neatly penned or barely legible, they all share one thing in common — each contains a hint pointing to the whereabouts of a hidden treasure.
desc2:
Hey, wanna play a game?
If you can find the <H>biggest gem</> around here, I'll give you a reward!

name: Icelake Ⅴ
desc: A collection of enigmatic pages discovered by chance. Some are delicate scrolls of fine parchment; others, freshly printed sheets with ink still crisp and dark. A few are no more than torn scraps from half-used notebooks. Whether neatly penned or barely legible, they all share one thing in common — each contains a hint pointing to the whereabouts of a hidden treasure.
desc2:
<W>There are no 100 pieces of Phoxene here.</>
 
(Beneath this message, some squiggly lines attempt to outline the mine's paths. The spot marked with a red circle appears to be <H>near the mine's entrance</>.)

name: Icelake Ⅵ
desc: A collection of enigmatic pages discovered by chance. Some are delicate scrolls of fine parchment; others, freshly printed sheets with ink still crisp and dark. A few are no more than torn scraps from half-used notebooks. Whether neatly penned or barely legible, they all share one thing in common — each contains a hint pointing to the whereabouts of a hidden treasure.
desc2:
I saw it with my own eyes — blue light, shining out from <H>under that fallen pillar</>! But there's no lighting rig down there... none at all. There's definitely something weird going on!
Like... maybe some miner worked himself to death and just... never left. No wonder no one's bothered to fix it since.

name: Icelake Ⅶ
desc: A collection of enigmatic pages discovered by chance. Some are delicate scrolls of fine parchment; others, freshly printed sheets with ink still crisp and dark. A few are no more than torn scraps from half-used notebooks. Whether neatly penned or barely legible, they all share one thing in common — each contains a hint pointing to the whereabouts of a hidden treasure.
desc2:
Hello, stranger, I am an explorer.
This cavern is absolutely enchanting, like something out of a fairy tale where snow fairies might live! The massive, crystal-clear ice pillars, the rugged old roots of a withered Heaventree, and the complex terrain that twists and turns like a natural labyrinth... it'll take your breath away!
If you've made it this far, don't give up now — the scenery up there is even more spectacular! I've left a gift and some provisions for you at the <H>cavern's summit</>. Keep going — you're almost there.
May you discover the same thrill of adventure that drives me. As long as there's life in you, let the journey never end!

name: Icelake Ⅷ
desc: A collection of enigmatic pages discovered by chance. Some are delicate scrolls of fine parchment; others, freshly printed sheets with ink still crisp and dark. A few are no more than torn scraps from half-used notebooks. Whether neatly penned or barely legible, they all share one thing in common — each contains a hint pointing to the whereabouts of a hidden treasure.
desc2:
Do you remember that day we left the city and wandered along the <H>lakeside of Lamenting Lake</>, wading barefoot through the shallows?
"Look at that tree with red leaves," you said.
"They're orange," I corrected.
"I said red," you insisted.

I'd saved up a few pieces of Phoxene — I was going to trade them for a real red-leafed plant, as a gift for you.
In the end, I buried them <H>beneath that tree with the orange leaves</>.

...Yes, I still think they're orange. I'm sorry. Leaves don't turn red just because you say they are — just like you won't come back just because I keep saying you will.

Maybe, when spring comes, the Phoxene will sprout and grow — like the feelings I still carry for you. Or maybe some lucky passerby will dig them up instead.

Either way, I think that would be a good thing. You always said good things are meant to be shared. If this gift I never gave ends up helping someone else... maybe that's a kind of happy ending, too.

name: Icelake Ⅸ
desc: A collection of enigmatic pages discovered by chance. Some are delicate scrolls of fine parchment; others, freshly printed sheets with ink still crisp and dark. A few are no more than torn scraps from half-used notebooks. Whether neatly penned or barely legible, they all share one thing in common — each contains a hint pointing to the whereabouts of a hidden treasure.
desc2:
Fact: if you keep an egg somewhere warm, it hatches into a chick.
So if I leave some Phoxene somewhere warm... they'll grow into a Heaventree, right? Then I'll be rich. Forever.
I'm a genius! No, scratch that — I'm a true visionary!

And guess what? I'm on <H>furnace</> maintenance duty. Hehehe... Tomorrow, I'll sneak my Phoxene in and start the hatching...

name: Icelake Ⅹ
desc: A collection of enigmatic pages discovered by chance. Some are delicate scrolls of fine parchment; others, freshly printed sheets with ink still crisp and dark. A few are no more than torn scraps from half-used notebooks. Whether neatly penned or barely legible, they all share one thing in common — each contains a hint pointing to the whereabouts of a hidden treasure.
desc2:
Everyone's got Snowcaps all wrong! They're not dangerous — they're delicious! Simmer them just right, season with care, and boom — gourmet magic, totally safe!
But that's old news. I'm done with boring, basic mushrooms. I want more. Something wild. Something weird.
I need the king of mushrooms!

So I scoured the sewers all day, and finally, <H>near the deepest sluice gate</>, I found them — a whole cluster of brand-new mushrooms! Just the colours were enough to make my mouth water. I took a few back. Already scribbling down some ideas for the first recipe draft...

They say people used to leave offerings to the gods for good harvests. So maybe... if I leave something under this mushroom patch, the great Mushroom God of Atlasia will reward me with even tastier treasures? Didn't have much on me — just a handful of coins and a few snacks. Gave it all. Hope the Mushroom God's not too picky...

name: Lonza Fortress: Volume Ⅰ
desc: A collection of enigmatic pages discovered by chance. Some are delicate scrolls of fine parchment; others, freshly printed sheets with ink still crisp and dark. A few are no more than torn scraps from half-used notebooks. Whether neatly penned or barely legible, they all share one thing in common — each contains a hint pointing to the whereabouts of a hidden treasure.
desc2:
The fortress won't hold much longer... Don't be a fool and stay behind just because of orders. You're not even on the official roster — no one will notice if you're gone.
There are spare supplies <H>near the airship</>. Take what you need and head home!

(The bottom half of the page is unreadable from dark red splodges.)

name: Lonza Fortress: Volume Ⅱ
desc: A collection of enigmatic pages discovered by chance. Some are delicate scrolls of fine parchment; others, freshly printed sheets with ink still crisp and dark. A few are no more than torn scraps from half-used notebooks. Whether neatly penned or barely legible, they all share one thing in common — each contains a hint pointing to the whereabouts of a hidden treasure.
desc2:
Temporary Supply Pick-up Point:

<H>Beneath the control console by the viewing window on the engine room's outer perimeter.</>

name: Lonza Fortress (Ⅲ)
desc: A collection of enigmatic pages discovered by chance. Some are delicate scrolls of fine parchment; others, freshly printed sheets with ink still crisp and dark. A few are no more than torn scraps from half-used notebooks. Whether neatly penned or barely legible, they all share one thing in common — each contains a hint pointing to the whereabouts of a hidden treasure.
desc2:
Hey, my dear ex-teammates — let's celebrate a little festival of our own!
 
Now, don't be hasty to shoot me down. I know the Fortress only allows Triumph Day... but surely there's no harm in a secret celebration or two, right?
Back home, we mark the first of April with the Snowmelt Festival: trinkets hung from pine boughs as the snow retreats, gifts exchanged beneath the trees, and a fond farewell to winter as spring draws near.
You all remember that pine in the <H>Simulated Battlefield</>, don't you? The one we riddled with bullet holes and cordite burns during drills? If you squint, I'd say those count as decorations. Next week just happens to be your training rotation — and I may have buried a little something <H>beneath that tree by the water</>. Volunteer for post-training clean-up and "accidentally" dig them up, yeah~?
(One each — no hoarding! I'll be watching, 0^0)
 
Even though I've been transferred to another squad, we'll always be best buds!

name: Mistwharf (Ⅰ)
desc: A collection of enigmatic pages discovered by chance. Some are delicate scrolls of fine parchment; others, freshly printed sheets with ink still crisp and dark. A few are no more than torn scraps from half-used notebooks. Whether neatly penned or barely legible, they all share one thing in common — each contains a hint pointing to the whereabouts of a hidden treasure.
desc2:
Ughh... A few days ago, trying to show off in front of my friends, I climbed all the way up onto the head of the Bi'an statue <H>behind the Admonition Stele</>. Now I've come down with a cold and taken a nasty fall. Feels like punishment catching up with me...
I've left all of this month's pocket money at <H>Lord Bi'an's feet</>. Really hope Lord Bi'an won't hold it against me...

name: Mistwharf (Ⅱ)
desc: A collection of enigmatic pages discovered by chance. Some are delicate scrolls of fine parchment; others, freshly printed sheets with ink still crisp and dark. A few are no more than torn scraps from half-used notebooks. Whether neatly penned or barely legible, they all share one thing in common — each contains a hint pointing to the whereabouts of a hidden treasure.
desc2:
...

21 September
I felt like trying my luck today, so I opened five Lucky Eggs. The first four were nothing special: a box of toothpicks, a rag, a packet of Skylily seeds, and some throat lozenges. But the last one actually turned out to be a packet of fine Mistwharf Green Tea!
 Lunocarp said my luck was pretty good... could I really be Lady Luck's favourite after all!?
 Might try a few more when I get the chance.

...

27 September
Opened ten Lucky Eggs today. Got three sachets, a voucher for osmanthus cakes, two discount coupons that each take seven silver off a better theatre seat (and they don't even stack!), a wooden brush, a hundred grams of dried peafowl droppings — the note says it's medicinal, but it's honestly just disgusting, so I'll probably bury it in the field when I get home — plus a block of ink and a box of matches.
 Darn it... not a single rare item these past few days! If it weren't for how cute Lunocarp is, I really wouldn't bother opening another one.

28 September
Lunocarp talked me into opening more than twenty Lucky Eggs today. She said I'd hit the guarantee and could get a "super rare" one. And what was inside? Two slips of paper, pet food, and some kid stuff!!!
What a rip-off! Why doesn't Bi'an step in and do something about it!?
I'm done. I'm never opening another Lucky Egg again!

In a minute I'm throwing the rubbish straight into the <H>lotus pond</> to feed the fish!

name: Mistwharf (Ⅲ)
desc: A collection of enigmatic pages discovered by chance. Some are delicate scrolls of fine parchment; others, freshly printed sheets with ink still crisp and dark. A few are no more than torn scraps from half-used notebooks. Whether neatly penned or barely legible, they all share one thing in common — each contains a hint pointing to the whereabouts of a hidden treasure.
desc2:
I am but an old wanderer of the Wuqiongzang Sect. By chance I came upon this quiet, hidden place and made it my training ground.
Now, having lived more than seventy years, it is time for these old bones to retire from the martial world. You who have found this note — to reach this place, you must possess uncommon aptitude and no small measure of courage.
I have buried a treasured martial manual <H>beneath the apricot tree in the rear court of the Hall of Ephemerality</>.
Follow its teachings, and within half a month you will cross water without leaving a trace; train for a further half-month, and a thousand miles will be but a single day's journey to you.

I leave this manual to you now. May it carry you swiftly towards the peak of your art.

name: Mistwharf (Ⅳ)
desc: A collection of enigmatic pages discovered by chance. Some are delicate scrolls of fine parchment; others, freshly printed sheets with ink still crisp and dark. A few are no more than torn scraps from half-used notebooks. Whether neatly penned or barely legible, they all share one thing in common — each contains a hint pointing to the whereabouts of a hidden treasure.
desc2:
Ever since our debate that day, one thing has become clear to me: if we stay in Haze Market, we will never know what freedom truly is, nor what it costs.

What we do here — all the little tricks and the loopholes we exploit — are merely ways of bending the rules without ever going beyond them. I don't want freedom that lives on compromise. There must be a freedom in this world that needs no cunning and no pretence... and I want to prove it exists. So I have to go — beyond the mountain we've looked to so many times, and further still, to heights neither of us has yet seen. Even if it means becoming a wanderer, cut loose from the world.

By the time you read this, I will be far away. I've left a few gifts <H>on the old boat by the water</> where we always played. Forgive me for leaving without a proper farewell, but I promise you this: we will meet again, on the day I find my answer.

name: Mistwharf (Ⅴ)
desc: A collection of enigmatic pages discovered by chance. Some are delicate scrolls of fine parchment; others, freshly printed sheets with ink still crisp and dark. A few are no more than torn scraps from half-used notebooks. Whether neatly penned or barely legible, they all share one thing in common — each contains a hint pointing to the whereabouts of a hidden treasure.
desc2:
I'd heard the Gritblight Expanse was brutally dangerous, and after today's wandering... well, it really is — terrifying at times, but thrilling all the same. Look closely and the place even has a strange sort of beauty to it; if not for the Filthoids running wild, it might pass for a scenic spot.

But with nothing around me except rock and deadwood, it's far too easy to lose your bearings. I left a pack behind earlier when I stopped to rest — I'm fairly sure it was in some <H>cave</>... but after circling the area for ages, I still can't find the entrance. At this rate, night will catch me out here.

Forget it. Whoever comes across it can have it...

name: Haojing: Ⅰ
desc: A collection of enigmatic pages discovered by chance. Some are delicate scrolls of fine parchment; others, freshly printed sheets with ink still crisp and dark. A few are no more than torn scraps from half-used notebooks. Whether neatly penned or barely legible, they all share one thing in common — each contains a hint pointing to the whereabouts of a hidden treasure.
desc2:
Cassia and sandalwood breathe their fragrance free;
orchid and musk sweeten the breeze.
Ask where the hidden treasure may be,
and the shepherd boy points to the golden tree.

name: Haojing: Ⅱ
desc: A collection of enigmatic pages discovered by chance. Some are delicate scrolls of fine parchment; others, freshly printed sheets with ink still crisp and dark. A few are no more than torn scraps from half-used notebooks. Whether neatly penned or barely legible, they all share one thing in common — each contains a hint pointing to the whereabouts of a hidden treasure.
desc2:
East of the city, where wild grasses creep,
lies a cavern with pathways running deep.
Night after night, searching bears no fruit;
yet the treasure lies where the grasses root.

name: Haojing: Ⅲ
desc: A collection of enigmatic pages discovered by chance. Some are delicate scrolls of fine parchment; others, freshly printed sheets with ink still crisp and dark. A few are no more than torn scraps from half-used notebooks. Whether neatly penned or barely legible, they all share one thing in common — each contains a hint pointing to the whereabouts of a hidden treasure.
desc2:
Southward, northward, east and west,
seekers roam each road in restless quest.
But where, at last, will the treasure be?
Above the water, beneath the dead tree.

name: Advensphere: Purgatorio Island
desc: Tokens said to lie scattered across Purgatorio Island. They stand as proof of courage, wisdom, and patience — virtues forged through the trials of adventure. Gather enough and present them to the Lunoxplorer in Icelake's town square to earn valuable rewards.
desc2:
An island beyond divine gaze and imperial reach.
Here, seabirds wheel above crumbled colonnades, and memories sleep beneath moss and the slow tides of time.
Venture forth — to witness, to listen, to explore Purgatorio Island, where secrets linger and echoes of the past still stir.

name: Advensphere: Icelake
desc: Tokens said to lie scattered across Icelake. They stand as proof of courage, wisdom, and patience — virtues forged through the trials of adventure. Gather enough and present them to the Lunoxplorer in Icelake's town square to earn valuable rewards.
desc2:
This is Icelake.
Before others define it for you, knock on every door. Search every hidden corner. Speak to every soul. And in time, you'll see the city changing — quietly, subtly — because of you. No introductions are needed. Icelake is you, and you it.
Step beyond — to witness, to listen, to become one with a city still waiting to be known.

name: Advensphere: Lonza Fortress
desc: Tokens said to lie scattered across Lonza Fortress. They stand as proof of courage, wisdom, and patience — virtues forged through the trials of adventure. Gather enough and present them to the Lunoxplorer in Icelake's town square to earn valuable rewards.
desc2:
A fortress untouched by rivers of iron or storms of steel. Now, only laments drift across its ramparts.
Yet no wall is truly unbreachable. The strongest bastions fall not to force, but to what stirs unseen in the heart.
Go deeper — to witness, to listen — into the Fortress, where smoke still hangs and memory refuses to fade.

name: Advensphere: Mistwharf
desc: Tokens said to lie scattered across Mistwharf — proof of courage, wisdom, and patience, each forged through trials of adventure. Gather enough, and present them to the Lunoxplorer in Haze Market to earn valuable rewards.
desc2:
Where land and sea fall away — the first breath and final hush of every trade route.
The incense-laced air hums with legend; beneath the eaves, whispers still drift. When the smoke lifts and dust settles... what will tomorrow hold?
Go forth — to see, to listen — and explore Mistwharf, a realm ready to leave its yesterdays behind.

name: Taixu Rune
desc: Glowing runes that hover in the air throughout Huaxu, believed to manifest when Taixu is awakened by incense. They can be collected using the Mechanical Nexus.
desc2:
"No one can resist what glitters! And the best part? You can get these cute little trinkets with prizes from Lucky Eggs. What a steal! This is why I'm the genius Luno!"

— Lunocarp

name: Advensphere: Haojing
desc: Tokens said to lie scattered across Haojing — proof of courage, wisdom, and patience, each forged through trials of adventure. Gather enough, and present them to the Lunoxplorer in Haojing to earn valuable rewards.
desc2:
In the Far East stands a great city, where pavilions and waterside halls raised by ancient hands have endured unchanged for a thousand years, as though they might stand until sea and stone are worn away.

Yet even songs passed down through the ages will one day find a new verse, and familiar tales will welcome new faces. Beneath the vault of heaven, the winds are rising and the tides beginning to turn.

Go forth to explore, to witness, and to listen in Haojing, a city soon to be made anew.

name: Essence Gelatin
desc: Gelatinous substance for crafting Track-Shift Modules. With a pure, water-soluble composition that deactivates at high temperatures, it demands exacting storage conditions. Its utility makes it worth carrying though.
desc2:
"Purity cuts both ways: a single component enhances its potency but also accelerates its expiration. My task is simply to adjust the impurity ratio, seeking a balance between strength and eternity. In fact, this principle applies not only to alchemy but also to any groups."

— Ecodna, Chief of Biological Applications at The Spathatoi, in "Disassembly and Reassembly: Biology of Filthoids"

name: Precision Magnet
desc: Material for crafting Weapon Track-Shift Modules. These specially treated magnets respond to diverse metal components at unique frequencies, allowing seasoned users to discern the most subtle irregularities in weaponry through their vibrations.
desc2:
"How fascinating! These little parts might seem dull to you at the moment, but once the fuse is lit, they will roar in the most spectacular way!"

— Oliver, Bomb Expert

name: Premium Dye: Lamenting Lake

desc2:
"The rubbish bins with little green flowers painted on them, near the west side of town — those are Leonie's. The ones by Glevum Pit, painted with grey stones are Edwin's. And those with the big yellow suns? All mine! But staring at the same colours gets boring after a while, so we switch things up now and then — that's the secret to keeping it fresh."

— Margie, Icelake Scavenger

name: Standard Hair Dye
desc: A dye made by blending various raw materials, capable of colouring hair in a wide array of shades.
desc2:
It is said that a fugitive in Icelake, once pursued so relentlessly by The Escort that he turned his hair white overnight from sheer distress. Ironically, it was this very change that allowed him to slip straight through their fingers. Thereafter, he took to wandering, frequently altering his hair with dye, until he inspired a whole crowd of ordinary folk to follow suit. From a distance, they looked rather like the signboard above The Asphodel — positively blinding.

— Camilla, exceedingly pleased with her own hair colour

name: Thought: Berenica
desc: Thoughts sifted from the drifting sands of remembrance. They carry the memory of someone — from the past, or from what is yet to come.
desc2:
"You have three lives.

Your first life is breath and heartbeat. You measure and perceive the world with your flesh and blood.
Your second life is connection and bond. Your soul dwells in the nourishment of family, a lover's kiss, and the embrace of friends.

name: Sigil: Berenica
desc:
A sigil for summoning Combat Partners. It is a staff to lean on in a battle, a pact of companionship, and an oath unspoken.
Heartfelt prayers shall be answered, and the desired one shall appear by your side.
desc2:
"Our tale spans over two millennia: a saga of embrace and massacre, of furore and mercy. History ebbs and flows like the celestial dance of the sun and the moon – constant and cyclical. In the grand tapestry of time recounted in these pages, I am but a mere observer, as insignificant as a flake of Hyperborean snow, a leaf from Aethyrie, a drop in Luca's waters, or a grain from Khemet's sands. Yet, in this immense cosmos, I harbour the hope that snowflakes will forge snowfields, leaves will form forests, drops of water will coalesce into rivers, and grains will gather to sculpt deserts. As all singular entities unite, history shall pivot in our favour."

— Betwixt Leaves And Branches — History of Atlasia, by Comnena, Chief Librarian of the Aethyrie Cloud Cavern Library

A sigil for summoning Combat Partners. It is a staff to lean on in a battle, a pact of companionship, and an oath unspoken.
Heartfelt prayers shall be answered, and the desired one shall appear by your side.
desc2:
"Our tale spans over two millennia: a saga of embrace and massacre, of furore and mercy. History ebbs and flows like the celestial dance of the sun and the moon – constant and cyclical. In the grand tapestry of time recounted in these pages, I am but a mere observer, as insignificant as a flake of Hyperborean snow, a leaf from Aethyrie, a drop in Luca's waters, or a grain from Khemet's sands. Yet, in this immense cosmos, I harbour the hope that snowflakes will forge snowfields, leaves will form forests, drops of water will coalesce into rivers, and grains will gather to sculpt deserts. As all singular entities unite, history shall pivot in our favour."

— Betwixt Leaves And Branches — History of Atlasia, by Comnena, Chief Librarian of the Aethyrie Cloud Cavern Library

name: Essence Thought: Rebecca
desc: Plucked from the shifting sands of memory, a complete thread of thought carries echoes of someone, from a past yet to come, or a future long forgotten.
desc2:
"You have three lives.

Your first life is breath and heartbeat. You measure and perceive the world with your flesh and blood.
Your second life is connection and bond. Your soul dwells in the nourishment of family, a lover's kiss, and the embrace of friends.
Your third life is thought and memory. When a reader sees your name upon a page, when a traveler hears it in a bard's song, when a child draws wisdom and courage from your story—your life echoes once more in this world.

All return to the Misty Sea, but not all truly die."

— Lady Nifle, Ferrywoman of the Misty Sea

name: Sigil: Void
desc:
A sigil for retracting a summoning. 
Although the gathering is brief, the longing does not cease, and perhaps the next reunion is just a blink away.
desc2:
"Child, do not revel in companionship nor weep at parting, for we are but fleeting moments in time."

— Lady Nifle, Ferrywoman of the Misty Sea

name: Statue Inscription
desc: The statue's base is marked with time-worn inscriptions, the faded text hinting at a hymn of praise to a deity.
desc2:
Fusa, the Goddess of Fate —
... of the Stellar Path, and the architect of the Threads of Destiny. 
As the dome and ... bear witness, we offer you our devout hymns. 

The radiance we see among the sprays of water was ... bestowed by you... 
Your believers gather at the hidden reefs, travelling to the edges of this remote island. 
People of ... bear witness to the revelation,
swearing to manifest their faith with the divine instruments. 
And so, the frozen melodies begi... to play. 

The first melody arises from the ... caves,
where the daylight spills out in rich waves.
The ... stone forms an elegant visage,
and destiny softly breathes within the encircling columns. 

The second ... is in a cavern with cascading waterfalls,
where the years have smoothed the cliffs ...
and the waters descending from the Nine Heavens have transformed into stained glass.
It is a place of scattered hymns, ... this sanctuary. 

The third melody sings of an ascending corridor,
extending to ... constellations, and the sun and moon.
Catching glimpses of stars beyond the constellations,
weaving a curtain that envelops all of Atlasia. 

Fusa, the stargazing Goddess—
Here we pay homage to you.
May you protect your faithful believers,
and grant us impeccable ... luck and happiness!

name: Catastrophe in a Bottle: Volume Ⅰ
desc: A yellowed and somewhat damaged book about alchemy filled with annotations.
desc2:
...
All readers know that the author has always lived a solitary life. 
The benefits of solitude are obvious. Firstly, we can crush and refine precious gems purchased at great expense without hesitation, and without worrying about these valuable materials being used as gifts to win the favour of others. 
(Note: Of course, gems can only fulfil their true value in the hands of an alchemist.)
Secondly, those who live alone will have more energy to experiment with the wonders of alchemy, rather than feeling deep regret upon finding their first strand of grey hair, and realising that one should not have been overly obsessed with fruitless love like the author. 
(Note: This sounds somewhat extreme, but in today's Empire, who isn't extreme?) 
And lastly, maintaining a solitary life can also prevent some unfortunate events from happening, like the following: 
Along the northern border of the Siberian Empire, there is a city called Icelake (Note: My teacher once went there, supposedly to visit a doctor named Enrique, but unfortunately I didn't inquire further), which produces Crystallo of Stella. It has a cold climate that makes it suitable for conducting research into the fire element. 
And the protagonist of this incident? Poor Vagim. He was one of the many alchemists in this region who specialised in the use of fire. He was 40 years old at the time, an age when many alchemists eventually achieved success. However, his greatest achievement at that time was not in alchemy but in having a child who was too clever and had a great interest in alchemy. 
(Annotation: A bit too harsh.)
One winter morning, at the insistence of young Igor, Vagim took his son to the alchemy workshop. Naturally, the presence of a child, which are unpredictable, dangerous, and uncontrollable creatures, resulted in an explosive situation in the alchemy workshop. 
The events that followed were not witnessed by anyone, but based on eyewitness testimonies and an analysis of the scene, it is believed that the following occurred: 
Vagim prepared the most materials: Beast Wax, a small amount of Phoxene powder, and a heating crucible. Under his guidance, young Igor followed the classic process and proportions, causing a small and continuously burning fireball to appear in the crucible. 
(Note: This is very basic, but this successful attempt shows that the child had some talent.)
For a child, Igor did remarkably well, and Vagim must have thought so too because he instantly praised his son. But unfortunately, this misled the young Igor, who thought that as long as he created a large enough fireball, he would receive even more praise. 
So, while Vagim was focused on preparing his own experiment, Igor, probably with the intention of surprising his father, added an entire block of Beast Wax to the crucible. 
(Note: Although understandable, this act was completely unforgivable.)

On that day, Icelake experienced its largest fire since its founding. And the epicenter of the fire was Vagim's workshop. The likely cause was the excessive addition of experimental reactants. Any novice alchemist who had thoroughly read the “Alchemist Safety Guidelines” would not have made such a mistake. However, we cannot blame a child for this. Without a doubt, Vagim was the one responsible for this incident. 
It can only be said that, as an alchemist, maintaining a solitary life is a virtue that benefits both scientific endeavours and the greater good of society. 
(Note: This is a painful lesson, so I should also be more careful in future.)

name: Scattered Diary: Volume Ⅰ
desc: An abandoned diary written with elegant handwriting but in a state of disrepair. Some parts are difficult to discern.
desc2:
...

September 14
I should be safe here. 
After all, ever since Brendan's expeditionary forces withdrew from here hundreds of years ago, this place has been an uninhabited island abandoned by the Church and ignored by the Empire. It's not marked .... on ordinary maps either. 
I can finally get a good night's sleep. ... must be exhausted by now as well. 
Tomorrow, I need to hide ... more discreetly and thoroughly explore the island. 
If I remember correctly, Brendan's expeditionary forces seemed to ... discover a massive temple. If I can find the ruins of that temple, then I can use it to shelter from the elements ...

September 15
I only discovered this island is inhabited today. How unexpected. 
Their accents have started to differ slightly from the common tongue, but we can still communicate in a simple manner. They claim to be descendants of fishermen from the Empire who came here to avoid conscription. 
I'm not surprised by their ... looks. They're probably worried I'll inform the Empire that ... , and attract imperial troops. 
Hah! When it comes to avoiding the Empire, I... Well, it's better to steer clear of them as much as possible. It would be bad if I brought them into this mess.

...

name: Surgical Log
desc: A fragmented recording capturing the last exchange between Psyche and Henrik.
desc2:
...

Psyche: Please, Mr Henrik, let me do this...

Henrik: <H>No means no. The anti-deterioration surgery is still in the theory phase. I can't use an untested treatment on you.</>

Psyche: It's because you're so kind... that the surgery remains untested.

Henrik: Hypnos' House exists to erase pain. If I experiment on you, how am I any different from the Legion?

Psyche: That's not true...
Psyche: You care for us, grant our wishes, and ease our pain. It's just that the pain hasn't disappeared — you've taken it all on yourself.
Psyche: The anti-deterioration surgery could be the only way to help all of us. <H>Even if it's dangerous, even if there are side effects, even if there's just the slightest chance of success, I'm willing to help you complete the research.</>

Henrik: ...Stop it. I just can't...

(*Rustle*...)

Henrik: What are you doing? Lie down...!

Psyche: Shh... Do you hear that? My heartbeat...
Psyche: I'll turn into a Filthoid soon. Maybe tonight, or tomorrow... And this heartbeat will stop. But... even if it's just one more day — I still want to open the door and touch everyone's faces; I want to close my eyes and listen to this thumping; I want to feel sorrow at the memory of your weary figure... I want to smile recalling my parents' love and care... I want to feel strength remembering {nickname}'s encouragement... and...

Henrik: Please... Don't cry. Don't...

Psyche: Aren't you crying too, Mr Henrik?

Henrik: I...

(*Rustle*...)

Psyche: I'm ready, Mr Henrik...

Henrik: ...Okay.

name: "Illness and Humanity" —  Excerpt on Deterioration
desc: A venerable medical tome detailing the causes, symptoms, and treatments of myriad diseases. Although many treatment entries remain unfilled, its cover boldly declares, "No disease is beyond human conquest" — a promise destined to be fulfilled by future generations of healers and scholars.
desc2:
...
Deterioration predominantly afflicts Charon individuals between the ages of seventeen and twenty. The cause remains unknown, and the condition is invariably fatal.
In the early stages, the patient's physiological indicators show no significant abnormalities. However, as the condition progresses, burnt-like markings, known as Deterioration Imprints, begin to manifest on the skin, with their location and pattern varying among individuals.
By the middle stage, the patient's bodily functions rapidly deteriorate. Externally, they may still appear normal, but internally, their tissues begin to mutate, resembling those of Filthoids. Eventually, the mutation exceeds the body's limits, leading to an irreversible collapse, marking the terminal phase of the disease. At this point, grotesque external hyperplasia occurs, erasing any traces of their former human form. <H>As the final phase sets in, the human existence ceases entirely</>, giving way to a nascent, predatory Filthoid emerging from their former shell.
It seems almost like a cruel <H>curse</>: those once blind may gain extraordinary sight as Filthoids, and the anaemic might manipulate their own blood as a weapon. Only in this monstrous form do they attain bodies capable of enduring such afflictions.
...

name: Foreign Tome
desc: An old, much-thumbed tome with exotic binding. Its pages are fragile, as if a mere touch could cause them to fall apart. Upon closer inspection, it appears to be a text on pharmacology.
desc2: Authored by "Fufeng," this tome appears to be a pharmacological text. Judging by the book's unusual binding, the author's exotic name, and its writing style, it seems to have originated outside the Empire's academic circles. Both the intricate annotations and the main text are cryptic, with the phrase "Crystallo of Stella" appearing repeatedly in the notes.

name: Letter from the Buyer
desc: A luxurious letter addressed to Henrik Ethelred, found in a drawer.
desc2:
"Mr Ethelred, I've had your family property inspected. Don't worry about the dust — a bit of light cleaning will suffice to prepare it for sale.
That being said, I understand this estate represents a century of family legacy. Though I know you haven't lived there since your wife's passing, it may still hold sentimental value for you. So before we proceed, might I suggest reconsidering its sale?
If financial pressures are forcing your hand, perhaps there are other options we could explore — leasing, rather than selling, might be a viable alternative. We can discuss this further at The Asphodel. Please allow me the opportunity to repay you for curing my grandfather all those years ago.

name: Unsent Letter in Reply
desc: An unposted letter, gathering dust atop the desk for reasons unknown.
desc2: <D>Your kindness is appreciated, but my mind is made up. Please proceed with the sale — it's for the children. </>A tenant has moved in. The sale can wait for now.

name: Dust-Laden Family Letter
desc: The latter half of this familial letter is smudged with water stains, rendering it illegible. The dusty page and the presence of the Hypnos' House eloquently speak of Henrik's choice at the time.
desc2:
Kid, I've heard the Legion has recently intensified their inspections. What you are doing now is growing more perilous. Perhaps it's time to drop it and permanently shut down the Hypnos' House.
I've always believed that Hayley's dignified death as a human being under your care was the best ending she could have hoped for. I also understand the significance of you opening the Hypnos' House right after you returned from Scarletriver and offering help to the kids who are suffering from Deterioration.
But I've already lost my daughter and my granddaughter. I cannot bear the thought of losing you, my son-in-law, the only family I have in this world now...

name: The Invincible Legion's Chief: Volume Ⅰ
desc: A serial novel with a sloppy title, set against the backdrop of the decades-old war between Hyperborea and Elysium, centring on the adventures of a Hyperborean boy. It's a favourite among the Empire's youth.
desc2:
Chapter 226, "Fierce Battle! The Scorching Whirlwind Shatters the Divine Light Herald"
Staff in hand, the Divine Herald of Elysium called down pillars of radiance upon the Legion's living tide. Valiant warriors and the very earth beneath them were torn asunder, cast against the crimson-stained ground. Shockwaves rippled from the points of impact, churning the smoke-laden air into frantic, dissolving vortices.
"<H>Death to the gods!</>" came the roar from the tide. Gaps opened by the light were swallowed in a heartbeat by the relentless advance. Beam after beam fell, and each time the tide of soldiers closed ranks — a grim testament to oaths sworn in blood, their will unbroken by the Herald's profane glare.
But every tide, no matter how fierce, finds its levee. The Legion's charge began to falter. Casualties mounted — first by the dozen, then by scores, cold statistics etching themselves across the field.
Then, as another pillar of light descended, a figure stepped forth from the ranks. "<H>For the glory of our Emperor!</>" His cry was cut short as radiance consumed him.
A silence fell. Another soul offered to the crucible. The soldiers braced, ready to pour into the breach left in his wake.
Yet no body struck the earth. Instead, the warrior lay cradled in the arms of a youth, his hand outstretched toward a vision of faith and hope — Legion Commander Leo.
His presence electrified the battlefield. All knew the scales of fate now rested with him.
"Commander! To your rear!"
Pillars of light converged upon Leo. He did not turn. He simply lowered the soldier to the ground, then lifted a single finger. The devastating beams dissolved into harmless sparks at his touch, merging with the smoke. A slight shift of his posture, and cannon fire from allied ships screamed overhead, striking the hovering Herald from the sky.
Leo advanced, a calm, deliberate force. The unbreakable dam had found its fault line, and his voice carried across the tumult:
"My apologies for the delay."
"This ends now, <H>you petulant deities in your gilded spires!</>"

Could the divine defences withstand the unyielding will of the Legion? Would Leo succeed in bringing the high and mighty gods down to dust? The saga continues in the next issue of The Invincible Legion's Chief.

name: Alice's Diary
desc: The diary of a traveller long exposed to the elements. Its pages mostly obscured by stains and smudges, only the most recent entries remain legible.
desc2:
Day 4: The blizzard has erased my tracks. I'm lost in the mountains... with no way back...

Day 7: With my last bit of strength, I made it to the mountain top. The blizzard's too intense; I can't find a way down. Met some other lost travellers up here... Hard to say how long they will last...

Day 8: Late into the night. Finally managed to get a fire going in a cave, safe from the wolves for now. She's stopped bleeding, but fallen into a feverish coma... It's so cold. When will this blizzard end... Such a pity that a beautiful and well-bred lady should meet her end in this godforsaken place with me.

Day 9: The weather's let up a little. Found a way down the mountain. Carrying her on my back, she miraculously came to. I promised her that we'd make it back alive together.

Day 9: She's become too weak to even sip water. She said she was cold; I felt the same. Cold and exhausted, we drifted to sleep in each other's arms...

Day 10: She'll never wake up again. Her last message, written in blood on the snow, will forever haunt me: "Take my warm clothes, and make it out alive"...

name: Field Notes: Volume Ⅰ
desc: Theo's comprehensive field notes that cover everything — the environment, plants, animals, and humans.
desc2:
Spotted an unusually large rat by the sewer. He had lots of cool scars and a weird little bottle strapped to his back. Could he be the legendary Rat Warrior from those tales?
...
At 3:10 PM, the Rat Warrior showed up again by the sewer. He was slow today, but not hurt – he was just waiting for other little rats to catch up. It seems he is not just a brave warrior, but also a dependable leader!
...
Awww! My Rat Warrior got caught by a beggar and made into a kebab!

name: Field Notes: Volume Ⅱ
desc: Theo's comprehensive field notes that cover everything — the environment, plants, animals, and humans.
desc2:
The horns of the Charons come in various colours and shapes. Does this have something to do with their intelligence?
...
The Charon man in the square seems nice, but he spends all day talking to toy figures – too immature to be an observation subject.
...
The receptionist lady at the inn has really long, beautiful horns. I've decided to observe her closely to explore the relationship between horn shape and intelligence.
...
Finally gathered the courage to say hi to her today, but she just walked away like I wasn't there! New hypothesis: the longer the horns, the ruder the Charon!
...
Met a polite Charon with just one short horn. I knew I was right! Marked as a primary observation subject.

name: Field Notes: Volume Ⅲ
desc: Theo's comprehensive field notes that cover everything — the environment, plants, animals, and humans.
desc2:
The one-horned Charon named {nickname} has officially taken part in my experiment today.
...
{nickname} didn't want to fill out the survey, so I've switched to observational study through shared activities.
...
While searching for the Rat Warrior's friends in the sewer with {nickname}, we were attacked. I noted {nickname}'s impressive combat skills! It seems the shorter the horns, the stronger the Charon.
...
The experiment was forced to a stop.
...
The experiment restarted!
{nickname} told me about the stories of the Hypnos' House and Psyche. It was so sad! I must study hard to become an amazing alchemist and find a way to clear the Deterioration so such tragedies never happen again.
...
If {nickname} is the child of a demon, maybe demons aren't as terrible as they're made out to be.

name: Annie's Letter
desc: A worn letter from Annie to her mother, frayed from time spent in a pocket but still readable.
desc2:
Dear Mother,
I'm not sure if this letter will ever make its way to you, but writing it now takes me back to the crazy mix of fear, thrill, and excitement I felt leaving home. Thanks to you, I've read extensively and learned about the many wonders out there in the world. However, it was under your watchful eye that I was denied the chance to experience these wonders, constrained to live as you desired. But now, having left home, things are different. The vibrant winds, the beautiful flowers, and the joys and sorrows of my journeys have deepened my understanding and appreciation of this colourful world. Recently, I've even made it near some snowy mountains – sights I've never seen before. So, I guess I will not go back home. You can think of this as the follies of youth if it makes you feel better.
With love,
Annie

name: A Lost Diary
desc: A journal unearthed at Glevum Pit, seemingly left behind in haste. Its pages reveal the author's profound remorse and some murky, possibly fabricated, secrets.
desc2:
...
Oh, how I regret it... I should never have told Hans those tales!
Like the one about a gem trader and a few bandits who were trapped in a cave deep in the mountains and died there a hundred years ago, or the story about the miner who, twenty years ago, ran off with the mine director's daughter, only to be killed and his body dumped in the forbidden zone deep within the pit, becoming a ghost that haunts the area...
Weren't these just old tales the miners made up to pass the time!? Why did Hans take them so seriously that he stole the key, ran into the forbidden zone, and never came back!?
Curse his curiosity... No, it was my fault... If only I hadn't filled his head with those cursed, eerie stories... It's all my fault...

name: Yellowed Diary
desc: A forty-year-old journal discovered on a secluded trail in the deepest reaches of Glevum Pit. The hasty writing reveals the simple yet intense desires of a young man.
desc2:
April 14
Many supervisors at Glevum Pit have been reassigned to other pits. No one's on night watch today, lucky me!
 
April 18
The soil here is unusually soft — I managed to dig down three metres in just one night! I've blocked the entrance with some old crates that have been lying around for over half a year. No one's going to notice they're missing.
My love, I know you think the legend about the gemstone is just a myth, but this is our only chance.
Wait for me, Hilin.
 
April 19
Feeling a bit off lately — dizzy, vision blurry, not much of an appetite. Must be the wound acting up.
Gotta suck it up. Time is ticking.
I saw a silverback vole just now. What a tough little creature. They can even make a home in a place like this.
 
April 23
Rough day. I finally made it deeper into the mountain, but now there's this massive rock wall in my way. Good thing I packed extra picks.
The pain's getting worse — it's like it's in my bones now. I can barely stomach any food.
My lantern's gone out, so I'm scribbling this in the dark — she's definitely going to make fun of my handwriting when she sees this.
But I've gotta keep a record of all this, so when I make it big, this'll all be part of my story.
 
April 24
I did it!
Honey, I'm so pumped right now! I just wanna see you and yell this good news right in your ear! While fumbling around in the dark, I found three skeletons and some stones — these must be the gems! It all adds up with that old tale about the gem trader and the bandits!
I'm gonna make it big!
Soon, I'll be rolling in it. And once I'm loaded, your dad can't say no to us anymore, and you won't have to marry that guy you don't even know.
 
 
 
 April

 I C ant g et O...
