 G em ... Cysta... 
 Wann... S ee H er

name: Angry Etchings
desc: A rubbing of words deeply etched into a wall with fierce emotion. The carver's anger behind each letter feels almost alive.
desc2:
I huffed and puffed my way up here, expecting a shiny treasure, and what do I find? Mushrooms.
Yes, mushrooms!!! Of all things — why mushrooms!!?

name: A Warning From a Wall Crack
desc: A rubbing of faintly legible text found in the crevices of a sewer wall, seemingly related to a question posed by someone living there.
desc2:
Address the issue and provide the solution, then you will find what you deeply desire.
Otherwise, you might end up like these Filthoids.

name: A Secret From a Wall Crack
desc: A rubbing of faintly legible text found in the crevices of a sewer wall, seemingly related to a question posed by someone living there.
desc2:
Address the issue and provide the solution, then you will find what you deeply desire.
 
People dump their filth and sins <H>into the gutters</>, burying them underground, comforting themselves with the illusion that nothing ever happened. Naturally, they remain blind to the <H>rats</> and hatred festering from them.

name: Say Goodbye to Poverty and Achieve Financial Freedom
desc:
An extravagantly worded flyer. Had you not witnessed the abandoned pit's sorry state for yourself, it might have fooled you for a moment. By taking this flyer, you spare someone from falling victim to a scam.
As for the bait in the box — consider it a reward for your good deed and take it with pride.
desc2:
Dear friend, congratulations! You've successfully passed our test and earned your chance to join us!
Enclosed, you'll find a piece of Phoxene as a modest welcome gift — yes, a "modest" one! Because this is merely an hour's yield from one of our new mining machines at Glevum Pit. That's right, our incredible machines can extract precious Phoxene even from exhausted veins!
History has taught us that the profit margins from new technology do not last forever! To stay ahead of the curve, we warmly invite you to come aboard! By registering as a member, you can lease our groundbreaking mining machines at a fraction of the cost. You'll only need to share 10% of your Phoxene haul — the rest is all yours to keep! The more you mine, the more you earn, with no limits — financial freedom is no longer just a dream!
Plus, the first 10 new members will also receive awesome gifts. What are you waiting for? Just sign up today!

name: An Addressless Letter
desc: A crumpled letter, seemingly soaked before. The envelope bears no address, only the recipient's name.
desc2:
My Dearest,
It's been too long. I am writing this letter from Lonza Fortress in Hyperborea, no longer as an imperial soldier.
After you left, I tried to move on as they told me to — but I couldn't. The Misty Sea took you from me, and cleared the fog that once clouded my vision. Suddenly, the world's true face and the grotesque truths behind the doctrines I once revered became clear. The splendid crown we once worshipped was merely a mirage, and I have now seen through it.
In my awakening, I joined The Forsakens. Just today, I ended the life of the imperial officer who ruined you.
I once vowed to follow you into the Misty Sea after avenging your death. But since joining The Forsakens, I've come to realize that the rot beneath the Empire's gleaming facade is even more horrifying than I had imagined. Our people are suffering, stripped of dignity, powerless against the abuse and oppression, for their vision is still obscured by the mist.
I cannot, in good conscience, depart from this world as it is. Forgive me for not fulfilling my promise sooner. No one should endure the cruelty we face. I must fight for a future where all Charons live with dignity in the light.
 
I will never forget you, and my love for you burns as fiercely as ever. When the war is over and our people are truly free... I promise, I will come to you.

name: The Forsakens' Pamphlet
desc:
The pages have yellowed with age yet remain undamaged. Someone must've kept it with care.
The cover features a portrait of a grey-haired woman, a pristine white flower blooming in her left eye.
The back cover bears the emblem of The Forsakens and the inscription: "May freedom guide our way."
desc2:
To all the proud Charons, do you still remember—
 
From the trunk of Laerad, our saga sprouted; from the embrace of the Misty Sea, our souls rise and rest. We are the cherished children of Father Ask and Mother Embla, endowed with powerful physiques, majestic horns, and indomitable spines.
 
Yet, the Hyperborean Empire has unjustly maligned us, trampling our dignity, tarnishing our reputation, and stripping away our rights, driving us into shadows of fear and oppression to make us forget who we truly are.
 
To all the brave and resilient Charons, despite the oppression and humiliation inflicted upon us—
The call to arms has sounded, and the hour of awakening has come.
We seek no false mercy from the tyrants; we scorn the crumbs from our oppressors. Born free, we are entitled to all the happiness the world has to offer.
 
To each valiant warrior of The Forsakens—
May you be blessed with the courage and wrath of Ask, to rise ever mightier against the mightiest foes;
May you be graced with the compassion and gentleness of Embla, to nurture solidarity and fight with one heart and one mind.
Let your pulses quicken and hearts swell with the tides of triumph,
And may we one day meet in a land where our brightest dreams shine realized!

name: Request for Additional Maintenance Manpower
desc: A rejected application, dated a year and a half ago.
desc2:
[Reason for Request]
Manpower shortage for fortress mechanism maintenance
[Details of Request]
Requesting the assignment of 14 technicians from the Aeolipile Alchademy for maintenance duties as follows: 5 technicians to service the central turret's firing and positioning modules. 3 technicians to maintain the fluid transfer well. 4 technicians to oversee the upkeep of supply transport routes. 2 technicians to conduct tests on the water pump control systems.
 
[Decision]
Request denied
[Reason]
The Aeolipile Alchademy has determined that the maintenance tasks described are of low complexity and do not require specialized technicians. These tasks can be adequately completed by the fortress's existing logistical staff.
 
[Additional Remarks]
To manage the manpower shortage, the command group recommends dividing the maintenance tasks based on their level of confidentiality. Classified tasks should be managed by military logistics personnel. Non-classified tasks may involve conscripting able-bodied Charon civilians from nearby villages under the Wartime Emergency Conscription Act. 
Should our current personnel be unable to perform classified maintenance, these conscripted Charon citizens may be assigned as needed, with all subsequent procedures handled according to confidentiality protocols.

name: Scrunched Note
desc: A conversation carried out via passed notes. The worn paper suggests this exchange took place some time ago.
desc2:
Buddy, you okay? You've been yawning a ton.
I had to stay up till 3 AM for extra target practice because my shooting scores were terrible :'‑(
That's rough... But you better watch it — if the officer catches you, you're screwed.
I'm trying to hold it in, but can't help it :(
Remember that Charon who talked back to the officer the other day? The one that fixed the tracks — do you know where he ended up?
Yeah, I heard he wrapped up his work early so they sent him back :‑| 
Nah. We're low on fuel, there's no way they'd waste resources sending someone out of the fortress.
Where's he then? :‑o
I saw a human finger in the military dogs' food bowl yesterday. What do you think?
!!? Okay, okay, I'm wide awake now! No more horror stories!

name: Some Forsakens Member's Journal
desc: The content of this journal suggests a certain laxity in the discipline within The Forsakens.
desc2:
October 20
The captain praised me today! I feel great! Starting tomorrow, I'm all in with my patrol duties — no more nodding off or cutting corners.

October 21
Snap out of it! You're a brave warrior of The Forsakens — sneaking off to fish by the bridge during your shift? What were you thinking!?
Tomorrow, I'm definitely sticking to my duties and staying alert.

October 22
This morning's patrol covered the northwest sector outside the fortress. No Imperial spies in sight, but I dealt with three Filthoids (two small, one medium), and spotted five pieces of trash <D>and two prime fishing spots</>. 
In the afternoon meeting, I caught the mechanic lady sneaking a look at a photo of some white-haired {性别2:man|girl} under the table. Is that her crush?
If even someone as important as "The Raven" could afford to space out like that, I guess it's okay for a little foot soldier like me to slack off once in a while, right? No way I'm giving up on my angler career — The Forsakens never quit!
Tomorrow, I'm hitting a new spot with fresh spirits!

October 23
Today's haul: a belt, half of a military boot, two pieces of Filthoid Carapace, and a bag of Imperial documents.
For crying out loud, where are all the fish!?

name: Request for Drainage System Upgrade
desc: A rejected application, dated two years ago.
desc2:
[Reason for Request]
There are recognized safety hazards with the current design of the sewer drainage system. A few days ago, a patrol soldier accidentally activated a mechanism in Reservoir #3, causing the water level to rise above the critical threshold. This triggered an electrical fault and resulted in injuries. 
[Details of Request]
Requesting technical support from the Aeolipile to refine and improve the operational mechanisms of the drainage system.
 
[Decision]
Request denied
[Reason]
The fortress has functioned for decades without such incidents, suggesting that the recent incident is attributed to individual error rather than a systemic issue.
 
[Additional Remarks]
This request has been forwarded to the Commission for Discipline Inspection. Effective immediately, new regulations have been added to the fortress's operational guidelines: Any unauthorised operation or mishandling of drainage mechanisms will result in a demotion by one military rank.

name: Triumph Day Leave Notice
desc: The only holiday the soldiers stationed at the fortress are allowed to celebrate.
desc2:
In accordance with headquarters' orders, all non-Charon soldiers are granted a half-day leave on Triumph Day. Specific leave schedules will be communicated by your respective units.
Important Note: Soldiers taking leave are required to attend the celebration ceremony at the simulated battlefield during one of the designated time slots below. Failure to participate will be recorded as an absence:
Morning leave: 09:00 to 11:00
Afternoon leave: 15:00 to 17:00
 
Charon soldiers will adhere to their regular duties as per the temporary defence deployment and are exempt from participating in the ceremony.

name: Lonza Fortress Operation Directive
desc: A crisp new evacuation notice that starkly deviates from the empire's usual formatting.
desc2:
Personnel not assigned to combat duties are required to finalise their handovers within the day and prepare for immediate evacuation. Ensure that all sensitive documents are securely removed.
 Patients and the injured will be evacuated on the first available transport. Subsequent evacuations will proceed in an orderly fashion according to senior command directives. Personal belongings should be kept to a minimum. Please notify your superior in advance if special arrangements are needed.
 Transport vehicle storage is reserved primarily for fuel and medical supplies. Heavy weapons should be transported only if deemed essential.

name: Simulated Battle Logs
desc:
Combat logs from the simulation console at Lonza Fortress. They meticulously detail the Imperial soldiers' performances in simulated battles, with candid assessments and suggestions for each squad.
The narrative shifts abruptly in the last entries, suggesting they were authored by someone from The Forsakens rather than the Legion.
desc2:
March 17
Participants: 7th Squad vs. 3rd Squad
Score: 3:1
Observations: The 7th Squad has shown significant improvements in combat capabilities, demonstrating solid team cohesion and defensive stability. However, their offensive efficiency requires enhancement — focusing on combined arms proficiency is recommended. The 3rd Squad displayed courage and decisiveness but lacked finesse. Prioritising defensive capabilities and intensifying physical training is advisable.
 
March 24
Participants: 2nd Squad vs. 4th Squad
Score: 2:2
Observations: The 2nd Squad executed a clear strategy, capitalising on their captain's exceptional skills through adaptive formations. However, their over-reliance on one individual poses risks. Developing broader tactical plans that don't hinge on the captain's presence is advisable. The 4th Squad maintained a controlled combat rhythm and executed their strategies with precision, yet their overall approach was overly cautious. Exploring more aggressive tactics could enhance their performance in dynamic combat scenarios.
 
March 31
Participants: 6th Squad vs. 3rd Squad
Score: -
Observations: <W>The session was cancelled due to unforeseen circumstances.</>

...
 
August 12
Participants: Green Onion Head vs. Pink Kitty Head ;)
Score: 4:5
Observations: Next time, I'm gonna crush you.
P.S. Gotta admit, this Empire doohickey is pretty fun.

August 14
Participants: Green Onion Head vs. Pink Kitty Head ;)
Score: 7:6
Observations: Off my game today. This one doesn't count! ;D
 
August 17
Participants: Green Onion Head vs. Pink Kitty Head ;)
Score: 5:3
Observations: I've been busting a gut fixing these gadgets all day — can't you cut me some slack!? Thought we were supposed to be family. :(

name: My Dearest Comrades
desc:
An informal register of military dogs maintained by an Imperial dog handler, carefully hidden deep inside a chariot's storage compartment.
Water damage has blurred the last few entries.
desc2:
1. Labby, 5, Male
True to his Labrador roots, Labby is a voracious eater with a heart of gold. He's usually well-behaved, though he once had a stint in solitary for snatching food from a "fur-llow worker".
Labby is brave on the battlefield, but his overly enthusiastic tail-wagging has been known to cause friendly fire incidents.

2. Sammie, 6, Female
Sammie, our stunning little lady, may not be the sharpest, but she's everyone's sweetheart. Known for her exceptional cuddling skills, she holds the title of Chief Canine Morale Officer. Every time I sneak her out to let fellow soldiers pet her, she brightens everyone's day effortlessly.
She's not cut out for complex tasks, but she's a pro at finding supplies (especially food).

3. Kollie, 8, Female
The alpha of the pack. Kollie is exceptional in every way, especially in intelligence. She's a master at finding the safest and most efficient routes.
But being too smart can have a downside — her brilliance sometimes eclipses the commander... It's no surprise she hasn't climbed the ranks despite her years of dedicated service.

<D>4.</>


If I had known that one day I'd have to say goodbye to all of you, I would never have kept these notes that now only bring tears.
My sweet pups, my silly children... you didn't have a nation to serve or a mission to fulfil, why did you give it all...?

In your next lives, may you be pampered family dogs in noble households... or better yet, may you be free-born in the wild, living lives full of joy, far from the reaches of human cruelty.

How I wish… I could… with you…
…If only… if we… how wonderful that would be…

name: Emergency Medical Log
desc:
An emergency medical log stripped of formalities. It succinctly details the condition of casualties and the emergency treatments administered.
The handwriting on the page listing remaining medical supplies grows increasingly frantic as supplies dwindle, clearly mirroring the writer's escalating anxiety.
desc2:
Area A - Urien
Gunshot wound to upper arm. Arterial rupture.
Interventions:
14:43: Applied tourniquet
Tourniquet checks:

15:40:

Abdominal laceration. Tibial fracture.

name: Transcript of a Conversation
desc: Transcripts of a discussion within The Forsakens about a new recruit who joined after the occupation of the fortress.
desc2:
Katya Oen, 23 years old, originally from a family of engineers in Dismania. Both parents are Laurelled Charons at the Aeolipile. Six years ago, driven by compassion for other Charons and a rebellion against parental expectations, you left home to pursue mechanical engineering independently, aiming to alleviate the plight of the impoverished Charons. While promoting compact heating devices in Ovis, you were captured by Hyperborean soldiers during a labour conscription raid. After ten months of forced labour at Lonza Fortress, you were liberated by The Forsakens during our breach of the fortress. You've been recuperating under our care for over a month now, and your physical and mental health have largely stabilised. Our investigations have confirmed that...
 
Katya: Wow, thanks for raking over my tragic backstory right to my face — your group sure knows how to make a girl feel welcome!
 
Gracia: Thanks. We've verified all the information you provided. It's been confirmed that you're not an Imperial spy but the sole survivor among the labourers at Lonza Fortress. You are free to go now.
 
Katya: That's it? Nothing else you want to discuss with me?
 
Gracia: No, that's all.
 
Katya: Isn't this the part where you all start tearing up and say something like, "The Forsakens would be honoured if a brilliant mechanic like you would join us!"
 
Gracia: We did hope for that, yes. But considering the feedback we've received from those who've interacted with you, noting your reckless behaviour and tendency to act dangerously without heeding advice...
 
Katya: Whoa, back up a little — aren't The Forsakens known for their bold, dangerous approaches?
 
Gracia: ...I can't argue with that. But...
 
Katya: Wanna hear a little secret? You guys ever wondered why you took over the Fortress without a hitch? Did you really think it was all thanks to your clever tactics and combat power? Did it ever cross your mind why, an hour before the train breached the Fortress, all the alarms and communication systems suddenly went dead, leaving them defenceless at the worst possible moment?
 
Gracia: You did that?
 
Katya: Hee hee, those Hyperborean dogs, always tinkering with their gadgets, didn't even notice that the girl who looked like she could barely turn a handle was actually messing with their machines right under their noses...
 
Katya: Then, all it took was the right moment, and... Boom! A pleasant big surprise! I hope they loved it.
 
Gracia: I see. We'll reconsider your potential recruitment into The Forsakens.
 
Katya: Hurry up then. If you keep me waiting too long, I might just walk away, and you'll regret it!

name: A Healer's Journal
desc: A lost journal that belongs to someone from The Forsakens. According to the entries, the owner might be a healer.
desc2:
...
Today, I had to say a heartrending goodbye to little Joe Frank. After he coughed up the last bit of blood in his lungs, he quietly drifted off in my arms, reuniting with his parents in the Misty Sea.
While there's a faint solace in knowing his suffering has ended, rage consumes me over the horrors he endured. He was only 10 years old — how could the Hyperborean soldiers be so cruel to him after his parents died from exhaustion and illness!? When we discovered him, he was severely emaciated, weighing a mere 15 kilograms. It seemed as though a mere gust of wind could claim his fragile life. But what enraged me most was that his chest had been filled with blood — a clear sign of recent severe trauma.
D*mn those Hyperborean monsters! I can't even begin to imagine the brutality he must have suffered! I curse the mercilessness of fate — why couldn't we have found him just one day sooner? One day, and that fatal blow to his chest wouldn't have happened. He could have been playing with toys, giggling, like any other carefree 10-year-old. And I detest my own incompetence most of all — despite exhausting every healing spell I knew, I couldn't save him. Before we left for Lonza Fortress, I promised his grandfather I'd bring him back safe and sound, but now...
...

name: Opened Letter
desc: A neatly written letter that lies open on the desk, already read. It is addressed to Henrik Ethelred.
desc2: ...My dear friend, I'm retiring next year, and I have little confidence that the new head of the Security Bureau will look out for Hypnos' House the way I have all these years. I fear you will need to be even more discreet and cautious moving forward...

name: Overdue Notices
desc: A disordered heap of overdue notices scattered across the desk, all urging Henrik to settle his debts. It's evident that Hypnos' House has been under financial strain for some time.
desc2: "Mr Ethelred, please be reminded that the quarterly expenses of Hypnos' House now substantially exceed those aggregated by all inns in Icelake Suburb. While we are not in a position to question how your funds are being used, it is our duty to inform you that your debt has been overdue for two months. Should the outstanding balance not be cleared promptly, we will be compelled to initiate forced collection measures against Hypnos' House in the coming days."

name: Medicine Labels
desc: A stack of torn-off medicine labels, each marked "Sedative." On the back of one, a message has been furiously scrawled.
desc2: "Not enough, nowhere near enough... Must increase the dosage... much higher!"

name: A Piece of Scratch Paper
desc: A scrap of paper with a short poem scrawled across it.
desc2:
I see the sun sear the earth
I see birds plummet from the skies
I see bullet wounds gushing blood
I see the grave open its dark maw
I see maggots gnaw at the dead
I see the Misty Sea whisper in the end
It beckons, enfolds me
Guiding me towards eternal nihility

name: Psyche Frey's Profile
desc: A folder unearthed from the file cabinets. It bears Psyche's photo and details her time at the Hypnos' House.
desc2:
Name: Psyche Frey
Age: 17
Symptoms: Intermittent blindness

...
When Psyche arrived, her Deterioration had already progressed to the mid-stage. Yet, she greeted everyone with such warmth. I wish I could believe the diagnosis was wrong — that she wasn't suffering from Deterioration, and that her life could somehow get back on track.
...
She keeps the flowers her parents brought her by her bedside, even though it leaves her barely any space to sleep or even stand.
...
I cleared out a better-lit room on the second floor. Hopefully, Psyche and her flowers will be more comfortable there.
...
She really loves flowers. Every day, she tends to them with care and shares them with the other children. If it weren't for the shadow of Deterioration, she would have taken care of the Flowers of Solicitude even better than her parents ever did.
...
Today, Psyche gave me a flower too. Her peaceful smile reminded me of you, Hayley...
...
Psyche saw me frowning over the finances today and wouldn't stop pestering me until I told her about Hypnos' House's financial struggles.
(Note: Must reply to the buyer soon. Can't let the children keep worrying about this.)
...
Psyche cleaned out the old house and even rented it to some kid with a shady background... I just hope that kid doesn't stir up trouble for Hypnos' House.
...
<H>Psyche told me she wished to live longer as a human — even if just for one more day. I was both relieved and furious to hear that. I felt relieved because Psyche finally opened up, after trying to be strong for so long.</>
<H>I felt furious because of that blasted kid! I don't know what that little rascal said to her, but giving false hope to someone who's destined to leave the world soon — that's the cruellest thing one could do.</>
<H>If you don't have what it takes to save Psyche, then leave her alone!</>
(Note: The anti-Deterioration drug is nearly ready. Fate... please have mercy on her for once...)
...

name: Elisa Taylor's Profile
desc: A folder unearthed from the file cabinets. It bears Elisa's photo and details her time at the Hypnos' House.
desc2:
Name: Elisa Taylor
Age: 17
Symptoms: Fading sense of taste

...
Unlike many of the other children, who cried constantly, Elisa has been eerily calm — almost aloof. When discussing her loss of taste, she dismissively remarked that food was merely sustenance and that flavour meant nothing to her. She even told her mother not to bother bringing her here, stating she'd be fine with a swift end at the hands of the soldiers. Elisa accepted her fate with unsettling tranquility, as if she'd been preparing for death her entire life.
...
Elisa seems to enjoy writing. Every day, she sits by the window, scribbling poems. Her poems are cryptic and difficult to understand, but the wording suggests her mental state is far from stable.
...
After a long conversation with Psyche, Elisa smiled — a rare sight. Until then, I feared her illness had taken away her ability to smile.
...

name: Hunt Clark's Profile
desc: A folder unearthed from the file cabinets. It bears Hunt's photo and details his time at the Hypnos' House.
desc2:
Name: Hunt Clark
Age: 18
Symptoms: Intermittent deafness

...
Emotionally, Hunt has been relatively stable, largely due to Mia's unwavering support. By the time he arrived, his Deterioration had already reached an advanced stage. Today, when I had to tell him his time was running out, this young man, taller than me, broke down, crying and pleading for a chance at life. He's only eighteen — with loving parents, devoted mentors, and a newfound love. It broke my heart, but I had to steel myself and remind him of the harsh reality: this is his destined fate. In truth, I was preparing to restart trials for an anti-Deterioration drug, but with high risks and no guarantees, I couldn't give him false hope. The cruellest thing in this world isn't despair — it's offering hope, only to take it away later.
...
Mia clutched the pocket watch Hunt had given her, tears streaming down her face as she softly hummed a tune, even though Hunt could no longer hear her. He passed away with a faint smile, seemingly at peace. I believe he didn't suffer, but he left so suddenly — before I could find the Crystallo of Stella to complete the drug...

name: Hive Mind
desc:
A collection of urban legends originally published in a now-defunct tabloid. In an empire ruled by alchemy and brute force, such tales weren't even worthy of dinner-table mockery.
Among its stories are "The Driverless Bus One Must Never Board After Ten" and "There Are No Pure Black Cats in Icelake." The tale presented here follows a man who believes humanity is nothing more than a colony of ants bred in captivity.
desc2:
I am a doctor. Formally trained under the Imperial education system, I, of course, never believed in ghost stories. I'm not writing this account of my final patient for fame or recognition. I do so only because... tomorrow, I will be dead.

It began the night before dawn. I was roused by a frantic knock at the door. The man outside was pale, soaked in cold sweat, his pyjamas still creased from sleep. At first, I took him for yet another poor soul fresh from a nightmare. But the look in his eyes deeply unsettled me: disgust, fear — and perhaps even... a visceral loathing.

I composed myself and offered him a cup of tea to calm his nerves. He took a sip, then spat it out at once. Had he not been a regular patient, I might have thrown him out on the spot. Instead, I waved off his apology and gently asked about the nightmare. After a few long, ragged breaths, he gave no explanation — only a question:
"Do you think I'm human?"

An absurd question. Biologically, sociologically — the man before me was undeniably human. But in his dream, he had become an ant bred in captivity.

He lived in filth beneath the ground, breathing foul air. His twisted body writhed as he gnawed on carrion and insect husks. He fought for scraps of space and garbage like an actor in a grotesque pantomime of survival — no different from the other mindless ants that swarmed around him.

Imagine placing a human mind inside the body of an ant. The result, unsurprisingly, was madness. It spat out the rotten meat, tore into its fellow ants with its mandibles, and cried out for salvation — but all it could do was twitch its antennae and scream in silence.

It tried to look up — but saw only countless emotionless eyes, <H>blank and pale as moonlight</>. It tried to flee, but everywhere it turned, there was only rot and crawling bodies. It tried to die — but instead, it was reborn, again and again, in blinding, incomprehensible light, until even its own body ceased to obey. Like all the other "normal" ants, it awoke, matured, and slept — drifting through an endless cycle, numbed by the haze of a thousand meaningless years...

By then, it could speak no further. I prescribed a few calming herbs and personally walked it out of the clinic. I never imagined it would go home, kill its wife and children, and then take its own life.

The Escort's official case file was neat and thorough. Yet I know — this isn't over. Because I saw them too: those eyes, <H>blank and pale as moonlight</>...

name: Crumpled Leaflet from The Forsakens
desc: A sheet of parchment bearing the crest of the Forsakens. It appears to have been hastily balled up and tossed into the sewers. Across the bottom edge runs a single line in cramped script: "May vengeance guide our path forward."
desc2:
Fellow Charons of Icelake — perhaps you scarcely remember any of this...

The headsmen and liars of Hyperborea seized the city-state built by our ancestors. A proud people was reduced to numb, obedient slaves.

They gouged out our eyes so we could no longer seek the truths the Empire hides. They tore out our tongues so we could no longer cry defiance. They shattered our fangs so we would kneel — and chew the scraps the Solarian so "graciously" drop at our feet.

And then, with shameless pomp, they called it order and prosperity — raising a blood‑soaked monument atop the bones of Charons.

But no more. The hour has come, my kin! Submission brings no peace. Only blood restores justice. No more silence. No more compromise. Let the Solarian feel our pain — Only then can we reclaim the peace, dignity, and future that rightfully belong to the Charon.

name: Prop Log – Galea Theatre
desc: A detailed log maintained by the backstage crew, documenting prop management at the Galea Theatre over the past two weeks.
desc2:
8-Oct
Organized: Costumes and sleeping bags.
Logged by: Mondry
(Note: Food supplies are running low. <H>We'll need to bring in another batch soon to prepare for the upcoming month-long intensive rehearsals.</>)
...
12-Nov
Replaced: Three new microphones.
Logged by: Grinde
(Note: One microphone produces an unusually loud sound, but Director Putsch insisted that it remain as is.)
14-Nov
Updated: Red curtain installed; gold curtain returned to storage.
Logged by: Bell
...
24-Nov
Retrieved: Five missing wigs.
Logged by: Bell
(Note: The dressing room corners are cluttered and seem to hide all sorts of things. I'll clean them out today.)
25-Nov
Organized: Fifteen flower crowns; nine pairs of riding boots.
Logged by: Mondry

name: Emperor's Signet Ring
desc: A medal forged entirely of pure gold. According to the accompanying commendation letter, this honour is reserved for soldiers whose contributions to the Empire are deemed exceptional beyond measure.
desc2:
Recipient: <H>Rhythm Fischer</>, Icelake Escort, 6th Legion, Cocytus Region

For demonstrating decisive leadership, exemplary bravery, and exceptional operational efficiency in multiple <H>Filthoid-clearing</> campaigns across the years.
For her irreplaceable role in upholding public order and safeguarding the people of Icelake.

Upon the assessment of the Legion, and by the decree of His Majesty Julius, Rhythm Fischer is hereby awarded the Emperor's Signet Ring, and formally promoted to the rank of Warrant Officer. Let her serve as an inspiration to all soldiers, urging them to strive ever higher for the Empire's glory.

All glory to our Emperor.

name: Aged Newspaper
desc: Yellowed with age and buried beneath a heap of old clutter, this newspaper recounts a tragedy that took place in Icelake years ago.
desc2:
<H>Deteriorators Are Exceptionally Dangerous — Do Not Be Fooled by Their Appearance!</>
On September 24th, an egregious case of Deterioration occurred in Icelake, with devastating consequences. Following an comprehensive investigation by the 6th Legion's Escort Unit, the details of the tragedy have now been confirmed:
On September 13th, local residents Mr and Mrs Fischer encountered a gravely injured young man, Robie Brown, collapsed by the roadside near Lamenting Lake. Acting out of compassion, they brought him into their home and cared for him.
However, Robie Brown was a Deteriorator — one who had evaded the Empire's routine screenings and fled to the outskirts of the city. While receiving aid from the Fischers, Brown deliberately concealed his condition. Ten days later, he succumbed to the transformation, becoming a Filthoid. The resulting massacre in Icelake's southern district claimed the lives of dozens, including Mr and Mrs Fischer. The 6th Legion's Escort responded swiftly and succeeded in subduing the threat — but not before the damage was done.

The incident resulted in 18 deaths (including 3 Solarian citizens) and 34 injuries. Citizens are reminded: under no circumstances should you provide shelter to unidentified Charon individuals. If you suspect someone of being a Deteriorator, report them to the Security Bureau immediately. Deteriorators are — and will remain — humanity's enemies. No exceptions. Harbouring Deteriorators or concealing their condition is a capital offence under Article 54 of the Hyperborean Criminal Code, punishable by death.

name: A Brawl at the Galea Theatre
desc: A handwritten record transcribed by Rhythm, describing a brawl that broke out mid-performance at the Galea Theatre two years ago.
desc2:
Brawl at Galea Theatre

Date: October 9th, 8:30 PM

Filed by: Letizia Putsch, Director of the Magic Flute Troupe

Involved Parties: Parsifal Snowfield (Lead Performer), Susanna Rossie (Lead Performer), Mathew Bernard (Audience), Feeley Francisco (Audience)
...

Incident Summary: A physical altercation reportedly broke out between troupe members and two front-row audience members. Alleged assault of performers by said audience members. (Several pages of the incident report appear to have been torn out.)

Conclusion: Evidence found to be insufficient. Case dismissed.

Remarks: Performances of Children From the Snowfield have been suspended until further notice. No resumption date announced.
I'd hoped to watch this one with Blues — to finally make up for the show we missed all those years ago. But I guess... that won't be happening any time soon.

name: A Journal Used to the Last Page
desc: Judging by the tone, this journal likely belonged to Blues Fischer. Page after page is filled with memories from his everyday life with his sister — not a single corner left unused.
desc2:
...
Finally put all the stuff Rhythm stored away back where it belongs. Come on — a secret base is supposed to be messy! If we follow her neat-freak rules, this whole place will end up looking like some boring museum.
When will my fussy big sis finally get it? The real thrill's stumbling on long-lost treasure hidden under clutter one day!
...
Passed the 6th Legion's entrance test — yay! And my request to officially use this abandoned maintenance room got approved too — double yay!
Can't believe the higher-ups said yes — just like that. No more sneaking in and out. Nice.
...
Gave the key to Rhythm today. We've already made a plan: once I get back from the 6th Legion, we're gonna make this place bigger. One room just for my tapes, with the biggest stereo, loudest mic, and the best harmonica money can buy! No real performer skimps on gear!
Another room for the posters I copied, my paints, sketchboards, and stuff. Aside from acting, I think I've actually got a bit of talent at drawing... Maybe a stage-prop designer isn't such a bad career choice either? Whatever — I'll just try everything whenever I get the chance!
Oh, and definitely a room just for our medals. A few years from now, I'm sure we'll both be Laurelled Charons with medals piled high. Gotta reserve an entire room just to display them properly.
And I also want to—! ...Ah. Looks like this journal's full already. Guess I'll have to pick up another one once I reach the inner city.

name: The Invincible Legion's Chief Ⅱ
desc: A serial novel with a sloppy title, set against the backdrop of the decades-old war between Hyperborea and Elysium, centring on the adventures of a Hyperborean boy. It's a favourite among the Empire's youth.
desc2:
Chapter 235 – My Heart Belongs to Hyperborea Alone

The celebration banquet had ended. Most had drifted into well-earned sleep — save for the soldiers still out on patrol. Quietly, the adjutant moved between tents, careful not to disturb her comrades' rare moment of rest.
At last, she lifted the flap of one familiar tent. Inside sat a composed figure that everyone relied on — methodically loading bullets into a magazine, one round at a time.
"Chief, we've already pulled back from the front. You don't have to stay on edge like this."
"When's the next battle?"
Leo spoke without even looking up, as if he hadn't heard her well-meaning concern.
"You crushed the Elysian forces in the last engagement. They're unlikely to move again anytime soon."
Leo said nothing. A tense silence hung between them. Sweat trickled down the adjutant's brow as she hesitated. Then, biting her lip, she reached into her coat and pulled out a bundle of ornate letters.
"Chief... can't you take a moment to enjoy life like everyone else — just for once? Look — here's an invitation to the Duchess's ball, one from the Princess's hunting party, and another—"
"'I am either engaged in pressing military affairs or occupied with guarding against infiltration from Elysium.' Use the same reply for all."
"But... that's the same excuse you've used eighteen times now..."
Clack—
Leo set the gun aside and stepped toward the banner of the Three Wolves hanging at the rear of the tent. His hand reached out, brushing the scorched edges — still bearing the bitter stain of battle.
"I understand your concern. And I appreciate their courtesy. But while we rest, Elysian raiders still strike at our borders, driving countless Solarians from their homes. They march beneath the banner of false gods, crying out for a purge of heresy — nothing but a pretext for butchering our comrades and kin. But we know the truth: <H>we are not heretics — only those who have broken free from the chains of false gods. Those who still yearn — for freedom, and for the right to reclaim it.</>"
His fist clenched. The banner bunched in his grip.
"Their so-called gods still squat atop our homeland. Until their divine tower falls, my heart will know no peace. If ever I am to enjoy life... let it be when I am shrouded in this flag after death, so that I may kiss it even—"
"Please don't say things like that!"
She cut him off. Leo looked up in surprise — but this time, she didn't avert her eyes. She met his gaze, steady and unwavering.
"Chief, I..."


Even the invincible Leo must one day face the battlefield of... social engagements!? What is it that his loyal adjutant truly wishes to say? 
The saga continues in the next issue of The Invincible Legion's Chief!

name: Bloodstained Journal
desc: A small notebook recovered from the sewers, its pages stiff with filth and dried blood. Most entries are now illegible.
desc2:
...
According to the sewer layout, they must've fled into this sector. Worse than I thought: our specialised scanners can't get a proper reading down here. Looks like I'll be stuck in this sunless maze for days...
...
Still no sign of them today. Nearly ran into the Escort, though. Could the Legion already be onto this? I need to get in touch with the Professor as soon as possible...
...
Even with everything unfolding, the Professor remains as composed as ever. I still have much to learn from him. When we meet again in the sewers tomorrow, I need to hold it together — can't let him see me as a mess again.
...

name: Momiji: A Chronicle of Rebellion Ⅰ
desc:
(These loose pages were found scattered in the theatre's corners, penned in Parsifal's hand. From the wear on the pages, it appears to be a script he studied often — perhaps hoping to one day take the stage himself.)

On the north-western cape beyond the reach of the Elysian Church, there once stood a duchy called Yashnia, a slender strip of land facing the Hyperborean Empire across the sea. A crossroads of trade and diplomacy, Yashnia balanced precariously between the Church and the Empire — until the Church annexed it more than three centuries ago.
Though small in size, the duchy endured for generations. Its dukes clung to power through a history steeped in blood: palace intrigue, aulic murders, and political assassinations. In the centuries since, wandering bards have mined Yashnia's crimson legacy for their dramas and ballads. Even the Empire — despite its official ban on the dramatisation of royal assassinations — permits such plays to be performed, viewing them as a fitting indictment of the Church's bloody past. Among these works, Momiji: A Chronicle of Rebellion remains one of the most beloved, praised for its sweeping music, elaborate choreography, and stirring depictions of battle.
desc2:
Act Ⅰ – Nocturne of the Swans

The tale opens during the reign of Yushino, third Grand Duke of Yashnia. Long before he inherited the title, Yushino was famed as a patron of the arts — immersed in painting, court verse, and letters. He maintained a grand troupe of dancers, each handpicked by the duke himself. Word of the troupe's brilliance spread so widely that nobles from both the Empire's capital and the Church's seat contrived to serve as envoys, if only to witness one performance in that seaside duchy.

Yet when our curtain rises, Yushino does not praise art or boast of his refined taste. Instead he broods over the bane of his sleepless nights: too many siblings. His father, the second Grand Duke, sired more than a hundred sons, and every one of those brothers now covets the throne of so small a state. Whenever Yushino closes his eyes, their faces float before him. He once tried counting them to lull himself to sleep, only to grow more agitated. On the tenth sleepless night, he made a decision.

He spent ever more time at banquets, drinking heavily in hope of a few hours' oblivion — meagre, but better than none.
When courtiers counselled restraint he waved them off, declaring: "If anything in this world can grant me rest — be it at a molten mountain's core, in a whirlpool at sea, or flickering on the rim of the sky — I shall possess it."

Thus, in the first year of his rule, from sunrise to moonset he held feast after feast, inviting his brothers to dine beside him. Pomegranate‑coloured wine never ceased to flow, nor did the dark veins in his bloodshot eyes fade. Beneath the crystal dome, youths in scarlet gauze danced the Swan Dance and sang without pause. Their floating sleeves swept across the nobles' cheeks, leaving them flushed — like clouds blushed by the sun before it sinks beneath the waves.
And each time, the Grand Duke would raise his goblet, wine running into his beard, his smile twisting into something grotesque. Then, catching his brothers in that hazy, entranced moment, he would murmur: "Would you care to bring one of these sweet-voiced swans home, dear brother?" And under the spell of wine and swirling dancers — who could refuse such largesse?

Thus a thousand swans flew out, one by one, into noble households.

Parsifal's Note:
In this sequence the ensemble dance is the centrepiece. Momiji appears here as one among many nameless swans. She must catch the audience's eye — but never so brightly as to break the unity of the dance. That balance is the true challenge.

name: Momiji: A Chronicle of Rebellion Ⅱ
desc:
(These loose pages were found scattered in the theatre's corners, penned in Parsifal's hand. From the wear on the pages, it appears to be a script he studied often — perhaps hoping to one day take the stage himself.)

On the north-western cape beyond the reach of the Elysian Church, there once stood a duchy called Yashnia, a slender strip of land facing the Hyperborean Empire across the sea. A crossroads of trade and diplomacy, Yashnia balanced precariously between the Church and the Empire — until the Church annexed it more than three centuries ago.

In the centuries since, wandering bards have mined Yashnia's crimson legacy for their dramas and ballads. Even the Empire — despite its official ban on the dramatisation of royal assassinations — permits such plays to be performed, viewing them as a fitting indictment of the Church's bloody past. Among these works, Momiji: A Chronicle of Rebellion remains one of the most beloved, praised for its sweeping music, elaborate choreography, and stirring depictions of battle.
desc2:
Act Ⅱ – Bloodred Meteor Shower

In the third year of Grand Duke Yushino's reign, nightly revels were no longer confined to his own palace. Every one of his noble brothers had fallen under the spell of Yashnia's sweet‑voiced， graceful swans. Their songs drifted beyond the high walls of noble mansions; even the ragged street children could hum a line or two.
To mark the third anniversary of his ascension, Yushino proposed that these long‑scattered swans be gathered at the celebration beneath the palace dome for a single chorus.
The courtiers urged caution. The dancers had not sung together in years, they warned; if their harmony faltered before so many guests, ridicule was certain.
But Yushino — half‑swallowed by his gilded throne — would not be swayed. In his mind, the voices of the swans and the pulse of his own heart were still one.

The celebration began as scheduled. Nobles filled the hall. The swan dancers reunited in the centre of the marble floor. Their faces betrayed no joy, no sorrow — for they were swans, trained to sway with the music, to shape their smiles to the tune.
At a single, crystal note from Yushino's favourite dancer, a thousand voices rose as one — clear and keen, like lightning splitting the sky. When the last chord fell away, silence descended — like the sea after a storm, so calm it seemed the revelry moments ago had been no more than a dream.
Yushino's brothers drifted into deep, sugared dreams. He watched, envying their peace. Since taking the crown he himself had never slept so soundly.

But tonight — beneath the bright moonlight — surely even he could find peace.

"Tatarnaga. Four hundred and ninety‑nine insults against the Grand Duke. Verdict: execution."
The voice from the throne was ice. One by one, Yushino pronounced the name of the noble who had scorned him most — and the long list of charges, meticulously recorded by the very swan dancer he had gifted Tatarnaga three years before.
The dancer who had long kept close company with Tatarnaga stepped forward, her serenity unchanged. A gauzy sleeve brushed the nobleman's cheek, just as on the night they first met. Then — a dull thud. His head, still wearing the soft curve of an intoxicated smile, parted from his body before fear could reach his eyes. It sailed cleanly through the air, trailing a fine red arc — a meteor of flesh and blood. Scarlet rain spattered down, staining the swans' pristine robes.
The night was young; the stars were already falling.

Yushino barely glanced at the carnage. He seized the hair of the courtier who had doubted the swans' unity and snarled: "Their loyalty has never broken pitch. Fool. Drink — and be as obedient as they are!"
Blood‑dark wine flooded the man's mouth and nose. He choked, certain he would drown.
Then — to his astonishment — Yushino's grip slackened. The Grand Duke sagged back, and a thunderous snore rolled through the marble hall.
Never had such a sound echoed in that palace, yet from that night onward it returned at the same hour every evening.


Parsifal's Note:
This scene calls for a solo. Traditionally, Momiji's sung by a soprano — but I've seen tenors pull it off brilliantly. I'd very much like to try it.

desc:
(These loose pages were found scattered in the theatre's corners, penned in Parsifal's hand. From the wear on the pages, it appears to be a script he studied often — perhaps hoping to one day take the stage himself.)

desc2:
Act Ⅲ – A Thousand Letters

"To my most revered, most tenderly pitied, most admired Grand Duke Yushino — you who once spent three sleepless years for the continuance of Yashnia.
This is the one thousand and first secret letter I have written to you — in loyalty, and in love. And as in every letter before, I write what I shall gladly write again, and again, and again:

I am forever your docile swan.
I am forever, forever yours.
Forever and ever and ever.

I imagine that, by the time you read this, a smile must have softened your weary face. One of the courtiers kneeling below your throne would stir at the sound of your laughter and ask what has pleased you so. You'd ignore him, drink half a glass of Hyperborean wine — if you drained it all, it would spill through your beard and stain your robe.
You'd sip while you read, deciding whether to finish the drink in peace... or smash it in rage.

Yes, I know you. Your face is etched into my heart and soul.

From the day you sent me to the Lady's estate, I began to write to you. A thousand letters, sealed with wax and entrusted to birds that knew the way to your hand. 
And each time I pressed the seal, I knew exactly what expression you would wear as you read.

Before the blood‑stained banquet where red meteors rained through the hall, you liked my letters.
Not just because I was your favourite swan, but because the Lady was unlike your other kin.
Though the other swans never spoke of it, I knew their noble patrons mocked you in whispers. That was why we were sent into their houses — to gather their sins behind a veil of dance.
But the Lady was not like them. She never uttered a word against you.
She said you were admirable — for banishing the brother who once mistreated her.
She said you were pitiable — for tossing and turning through the night over your nobles' crimes.
She said you were brilliant — for wrapping grand designs in feasts and song.

She spoke of other things, too: of Yashnia's moon, which she saw each night; of Hyperborea's snow, which she had never seen; of Elysium's flowers, which visited only in dreams.
But not once did she ask me to dance. Perhaps she had seen too many swan dances in your palace — or perhaps she had never known a real friend.
I was disheartened. Swans are born to dance — yet I was left to write, with quills plucked from my own wings.
And still, I hoped — that each time you opened one of those harmless little letters, the furrows on your brow would soften.
And perhaps that is why, on the night of that blood‑drenched banquet, she alone walked out beneath the echo of your thunderous snores.
I followed her out, as she stepped into the dawn. Her breath misted in the cold, her shoulders trembled — fear of you, or joy for your newfound peace? I could not tell. I only felt relief — that she had never once spoken ill of you. If she had, even had I disobeyed your order, the other swans would have torn her apart like ravens at your command.
From that day on, I was the only swan who never returned to your palace.
Outwardly, nothing changed: she still shared her stories and wishes for travels with me, and every fourth day I sent you another letter.
But perhaps... it only seemed that way. Before the sun rises, all is called night. But the midnight of your thunderous snores, and the final breath before dawn — can they truly be the same?

Since then, I imagine you no longer smile when you read me.
You buried yourself in state affairs: reforms, punishments, suspicion. You trusted no one in Yashnia who still breathed. Even birdsong was questioned — for daring to disturb your sleep.
The Lady was no exception. Her praise became flattery. Her silence, a hidden slight. Her advice, betrayal.
How could you?

Allow me to be plain: from my first autumn in her estate, she let me stop calling myself "swan."
By now I expect you have hurled your wineglass in rage, Grand Duke Yushino.
You saved me from starvation — made me your ever-dancing swan. But she is the one who taught that swan to be a person.
She never asked me to dance — because people are not swans.
To protect her, I was ever obedient, ever gentle, ever yours. Always fearing your fury would fall on her.
But your suspicion grew like mould in the dark. I defended her, again and again. Until seven days ago — when you summoned her to the palace... and she never returned.
So now, I ask just one thing:

Is she still alive?

I no longer wish to be anyone's swan. If she is gone, then I shall tread upon the shards of your shattered glass — even if my feet must bleed to reach you — until your blood spills like wine and dyes your robe crimson.
By the time you reach this line, I will already be standing before you, ready to pierce this letter — and your throat — with the very same blade."

"Raise your head and answer me, Yushino!"


Parsifal's Note:
Except for the final line, the entire scene is sung by Yushino as he reads Momiji's letter aloud. The performance must reflect the full emotional arc within the letter — from deferential restraint, to repressed grief, to seething fury. The true challenge lies in moving seamlessly and convincingly between Yushino's visible reactions and the inner voice of Momiji, gradually rising to its breaking point. It demands exceptional control.

name: Momiji: A Chronicle of Rebellion Ⅳ
desc:
(These loose pages were found scattered in the theatre's corners, penned in Parsifal's hand. From the wear on the pages, it appears to be a script he studied often — perhaps hoping to one day take the stage himself.)

On the north-western cape beyond the reach of the Elysian Church, there once stood a duchy called Yashnia, a slender strip of land facing the Hyperborean Empire across the sea. A crossroads of trade and diplomacy, Yashnia balanced precariously between the Church and the Empire — until the Church annexed it more than three centuries ago.
Though small in size, the duchy endured for generations. Its dukes clung to power through a history steeped in blood: palace intrigue, aulic murders, and political assassinations. In the centuries since, wandering bards have mined Yashnia's crimson legacy for their dramas and ballads. Even the Empire — despite its official ban on the dramatisation of royal assassinations — permits such plays to be performed, viewing them as a fitting indictment of the Church's bloody past. Among these works, Momiji: A Chronicle of Rebellion remains one of the most beloved, praised for its sweeping music, elaborate choreography, and stirring depictions of battle.
desc2:
Act Ⅳ – A Speck of Crimson

"That was only an acci—"
The Lady's death might indeed have been an accident. But even a swan knows: without Grand Duke Yushino's command, no gaoler would dare fetch the tools of torture.
And of all people, the limping figure now standing before him knew Yushino best — and hated him most.

So before he could finish the sentence, she drove her sword straight through his skull.

The tip of the blade first reached his tongue — a soft, writhing strip of flesh that split in two, bright red. It reminded her of a serpent's tongue. The Lady had once said she feared nothing more than the eight-headed serpent from Yashnia's ancient myths.
Then came something firmer — the upper palate. Heavy drinkers often complained of a burning sensation there. Yushino had drunk often, and well. Maybe his was tougher than most. Or maybe not — the steel passed through without resistance.
After that, everything was easy: the hindbrain. Some say it governs sleep. Years ago, Yushino scoured the land for physicians to cure his insomnia. One had told him the problem lay in his hindbrain. She no longer remembered whether that poor man had ended up with his skull smashed or his tongue cut out. Now, Yushino had suffered both. A shattered skull and a severed tongue — quite a poetic ending for him, right?
Before his bloodied lips could kiss the edge of her blade, she pulled it free.
A spray of scarlet spattered a folding screen; the fabric drank it in, the stain blooming like red leaves.

She remembered the day the Lady told her she no longer needed to call herself a swan.

It was an autumn afternoon, just before the frost set in. A northern wind from Hyperborea had swept away the last warmth lingering over Yashnia — only to spend all its strength in doing so. The sea turned bitter‑cold overnight. No nobles dared swim; no fishermen dared cast their nets.
Further inland, the farmers had just finished harvesting the wheat, yet still fretted that rain might come too soon and spoil the drying grain. Children, sent out reluctantly at the adults' urging, were tasked with picking up the fallen stalks — only to end up bickering over trifles halfway through. From the houses by the fields came the warm scent of fresh bread, baked with the season's first wheat. Cooking smoke curled gently from the chimneys.
Through that smoke flew the migratory birds bound south — save one small bird, a ribbon tied to its leg, winging the opposite way. It slipped through the domes and rooftops to deliver the four hundredth secret letter to Grand Duke Yushino.
It was his first year on the throne. Amidst sleepless nights, he had only just begun his long campaign — to purge his enemies and secure his rule. Perhaps the gods who govern the seasons took pity on his resolve and granted Yashnia another golden harvest.
And in that hush of ripened wheat, not far from the palace, in a quiet courtyard — a swan said no.

A cold wind stirred. The trees in the Lady's courtyard groaned softly, as if in pain. Red leaves drifted down like blood. One struck the Lady's face. She flinched with a startled yelp — like a cat caught by sudden darkness. The limping one reached out and gently brushed the leaf away.
The Lady's cheeks were flushed from the cold. She looked at her and said: "From now on, you don't have to call yourself a swan. Your name... will be Momiji. Only I will know this. Only I may call you this."

The swan hesitated. She agreed to stop calling herself a bird — but cautiously declined the name Momiji, afraid that if she heard it too often,
she might come to love it. And along with it... too many other things.

She could no longer recall what happened next. Only that, somehow, she had cried — though she never knew quite why.
Tears are warm at first. But they soon turn cold. And so do the red leaves — fiery in hue, cold in the hand.

Cold, like Yushino's blood already congealing on marble.

Perhaps it was because she hadn't danced in so long. She might have avoided the spatter, yet one drop landed on the hilt of her sword.
She tried to wipe the red away — again and again. But it wouldn't come off. And that brought her back to the moment when a red leaf had fallen onto the Lady's face. She had tried to brush it away, too — but hadn't been able to. As if she were waiting for someone else to do it for her.
She lingered again in that autumn, seven years ago — where everything had seemed well.
So be it, then. Let that speck of crimson remain.
She made no further attempt to wipe the blood away. Nor did she shy from the name Momiji any longer. She turned and walked away — unchallenged, and alone.

Thus closed the tale of Momiji: A Chronicle of Rebellion.


Parsifal's Note:
The protagonist's name — Momiji — isn't revealed until the very final act. When the play first debuted, this twist had tremendous impact. But now, after so many stagings, most audiences know it going in. It's a shame — there's nothing quite like the first time.
Here's an excerpt from the historical record. Might be useful...
"According to official chronicles, the third Grand Duke of Yashnia, Yushino, reigned for ten years. In the early years, he purged his political enemies and swept away many of the entrenched ills left by his predecessor, the second Grand Duke. But toward the end of his rule, he grew increasingly suspicious of his own kin. Eventually, he ordered the imprisonment and torture of his sister, resulting in her death. The very next day, he himself was found dead. By then, the fall of Yashnia — to either the Empire or the Elysian Church — had already become inevitable. That the Church ultimately took it... well, that's a matter for another chapter on court conspiracies.
As for Yushino's death, three theories persist: suicide brought on by madness, sudden death from chronic alcoholism, and assassination by a swordswoman named Momiji. The third is deemed the least credible — and yet, it remains the version most widely believed. This account is also said to have inspired the now-famous play Momiji: A Chronicle of Rebellion.

name: Silvercandle Hymns (Ⅰ)
desc:
A hymn sung at the Silvercandle Carnival, recounting its legendary origin: Soranus, younger brother to Dis Ⅰ, first emperor of Hyperborea, was struck down by the Charon. Yet after conquest was won, Dis Ⅰ chose not vengeance but peace, and held a great feast.
 From that feast is said to descend the Silvercandle Carnival as it is known today.
desc2:
Ⅰ. Overture

Hast thou ever heard of such a revelry,

Where profane soldiers and demon's progeny joined hand in hand?

Where the southerling and the nordling raised a song as one,

To hymn the silver peace ‘twixt Sola and Charon!

Tears of wax did drip from Sola's candlelight,

Upon Charon's face, naught but carefree delight.

They twisted their waists, they swung limb and limb,

With steps of dance, their joy did brim.

Through joy they reached madness, a fevered state,

Through madness, forgot sorrow and fate.

Through sorrow, bestowed upon the past its weight,

And at the end of past — a name to celebrate!

Soranus Galea!

He who took an ancient name, yet defied the false god's claim,

He who inherited an armored surname, to aid the Emperor's frame.

The younger brother of His Majesty Dis Galea, departed from our world too soon,

Soranus Galea!

name: Silvercandle Hymns (Ⅱ)
desc:
A hymn sung at the Silvercandle Carnival, recounting its legendary origin: Soranus, younger brother to Dis Ⅰ, first emperor of Hyperborea, was struck down by the Charon. Yet after conquest was won, Dis Ⅰ chose not vengeance but peace, and held a great feast.
 From that feast is said to descend the Silvercandle Carnival as it is known today.
desc2:
Ⅱ. In Praise of Soranus Galea

Northward! To lands afar from the false god's gaze,

Northward! To fields unbound by mortal chains,

Northward! To realms abundant with liberty!

In the third early winter since the Exodus,

House Galea pressed on, never to repose.

They swore to flee the Elysian Church's hold,

With silver blades against the world's end cold.

At the forefront of that argent tide,

His form you'd see, striding with pride.

His helm shone bright, a guiding star afar,

His steps held firm, like flowers unmarred.

His eyes gleamed keen, rare diamonds untold,

His form sped light, as dust on winds old.

Soranus Galea!

Treasure of Dis the First, the household's young wolf,

Whenever he drew his sword, comedy unfolded—

Victory assured, the battle's ending foretold.

name: Silvercandle Hymn (Ⅲ)
desc:
A hymn sung at the Silvercandle Carnival, recounting its legendary origin: Soranus, younger brother to Dis Ⅰ, first emperor of Hyperborea, was struck down by the Charon. Yet after conquest was won, Dis Ⅰ chose not vengeance but peace, and held a great feast.
 From that feast is said to descend the Silvercandle Carnival as it is known today.
desc2:
Ⅲ. The Gift of Fate
 
 From revelry did tragedy arise;
 
 From the eternal was born what must pass.
 
 South of Lamenting Lake, the snows lay deep.
 
 And those from gentler lands had never beheld such boundless white.
 
 Fallen feathers, ashen earth, lips pale as the ivory lake's milk-stone.
 
 What once was marvel at the snow became dread of death.
 
 Empty bellies growled, heralds of despair unborn.
 
 Even Soranus, fairest and steadfast,
 
 Scoured desperately for a single morsel.
 
 But not even Soranus could conjure wheat from icefields.
 
 He gnawed upon blocks of snow,
 
 Leant upon his longsword as a crutch,
 
 And ventured into the blizzard for one last charge,
 
 Hoping fate concealed a gift beyond the winter's end.
 
 When the storm at last relented,
 
 A village appeared above Lamenting Lake.
 
 With the last of his strength, Soranus knocked upon its gate,
 
 And gave thanks for fate's final, merciful gift.
 
 Yet perhaps, for he and his brother had spurned the gods,
 
 He knew not in that hour the first verse of his downfall was already writ.

name: Silvercandle Hymn (Ⅳ)
desc:
A hymn sung at the Silvercandle Carnival, recounting its legendary origin: Soranus, younger brother to Dis Ⅰ, first emperor of Hyperborea, was struck down by the Charon. Yet after conquest was won, Dis Ⅰ chose not vengeance but peace, and held a great feast.
 From that feast is said to descend the Silvercandle Carnival as it is known today.
desc2:
Ⅳ. The Snow-Owl's Ballad, Canto Ⅰ
 
 The snow-owl rejoiced, the snow-owl sang,
 
 Thrice it wheeled through the nighted sky,
 
 Seeking fattened mice to still its hunger.
 
 Yet beneath the vault of the Far North,
 
 No breath of life was to be found...
 
 Save for that place — 
 
 A hamlet of snow, a village of ice.
 
 The Charon hastened upon the lake's edge ,
 
 While from the south the Solarian sang.
 
 The fish cast off its cloak of brine,
 
 Unfolding blossoms of glistening fat,
 
 More fragrant than the buds of a springvine.
 
 The mash unveiled as its froth fell away,
 
 Revealing crimson draperies of the closing day,
 
 More splendid than autumn's dusk.
 
 Since the day Soranus struck the door of that village by Lamenting Lake,
 
 The feast where strangers became kin has never ceased.
 
 Every Sola laid down their sword,
 
 And embraced the Charon newly met,
 
 Praising their bounty,
 
 Giving thanks for their shelter.
 
 Even Dis Galea, ever wary,
 
 Exchanged oaths with the Charon's chief,
 
 Swearing to treat the Charon as brothers, as dear as Soranus himself,
 
 To stand as one against Filthoids, against winter, against every foe to come.
 
 Even the snow-owl, vigilant hunter, raised its voice in joy,
 
 And sought to alight upon the laden platters that it, too, would share the feast.

name: Silvercandle Hymn (Ⅴ)
desc:
A hymn sung at the Silvercandle Carnival, recounting its legendary origin: Soranus, younger brother to Dis Ⅰ, first emperor of Hyperborea, was struck down by the Charon. Yet after conquest was won, Dis Ⅰ chose not vengeance but peace, and held a great feast.
 From that feast is said to descend the Silvercandle Carnival as it is known today.
desc2:
Ⅴ. The Snow-Owl's Ballad, Canto Ⅱ
 
 The snow-owl faltered, the snow-owl cried,
 
 Six times it wheeled through the nighted sky.
 
 It longed to feast at the banquet...
 
 Yet as it poised to descend,
 
 A wall of spears and blades arose.
 
 Perhaps the wine had been too sweet,
 
 For the hapless Solarian forgot —
 
 The truth bound in the name "Charon": the Children of the Demon.
 
 Children of the Demon, bereft of all virtue, delighting in the defilement of oaths.
 
 Children of the Demon, sly and venomous, weaving their webs of lies.
 
 The salted fish was but prelude to slaughter;
 
 The goblet brimming but crimson-veiled malice.
 
 The Charon chieftain, raising his cup, loosed a baleful laugh —
 
 The kindly feast laid bare as nothing but a snare.
 
 The northern snow fell like Death's scythe;
 
 Could it ever suffer two peoples in peace?
 
 Golden hair dishevelled, silver goblets overturned, iron armour rent.
 
 Swords clamoured loud, driving ever closer upon the Solarian guests.
 
 Arrows sped in volleys, hounding the Solarian like a hunted pack of wolves.

name: Silvercandle Hymn (Ⅵ)
desc:
A hymn sung at the Silvercandle Carnival, recounting its legendary origin: Soranus, younger brother to Dis Ⅰ, first emperor of Hyperborea, was struck down by the Charon. Yet after conquest was won, Dis Ⅰ chose not vengeance but peace, and held a great feast.
 From that feast is said to descend the Silvercandle Carnival as it is known today.
desc2:
Ⅵ. The Snow-Owl's Ballad, Canto Ⅲ
 
 The snow-owl wept, the snow-owl cried,
 
 Nine times it wheeled through the nighted sky.
 
 It longed to flee the tumult —
 
 Yet cunning are the demons,
 
 Who beguile not only the bewildered bird.
 
 Even Dis Galea, who once struck down a false god,
 
 Deemed himself scorned by Fate,
 
 Doomed to an end unimagined.
 
 Only one carved a path through the tightening snare of the Charon:
 
 Soranus Galea, blazing with wrath at deceit.
 
 In fury he cast a burning candelabrum as a spear, piercing the armour of his foes.
 
 In defiance he swung a brimming silver goblet as a hammer, shattering the helms of the wicked.
 
 Before him, the Charon fell in heaps;
 
 Behind him, stretched a road of blood and flesh.
 
 It was he who had once knocked upon that door,
 
 And so he swore he would depart in whole.
 
 Dis Galea followed close behind,
 
 As though clawing free from a demon's ravenous maw.
 
 He rejoiced that his banner yet stood, unswallowed by the snow.
 
 But Soranus had spent his final strength.
 
 The demons overtook him, their blades came down,
 
 And from that noble brow there burst a white flame.
 
 The glacier crumbled, blood welled forth, hardening into stones of crimson agate.
 
 So fell Soranus Galea, sole brother of Dis Ⅰ.
 
 On the day the Great Migration began, he had sworn to march hand in hand with Death.
 
 Yet none foresaw that Fate would on this day bare its fangs in laughter.
 
 And the snow-owl, too, seeking its feast,
 
 Was struck by an accursed arrow,
 
 Its breath lost amid the bloodied waters.
 
 Alas! Soranus — hero who called for peace...
 
 He never lived to behold the birth of the Hyperborean Empire,
 
 Yet he became its first and truest hero.

name: Silvercandle Hymn (Ⅶ)
desc:
A hymn sung at the Silvercandle Carnival, recounting its legendary origin: Soranus, younger brother to Dis Ⅰ, first emperor of Hyperborea, was struck down by the Charon. Yet after conquest was won, Dis Ⅰ chose not vengeance but peace, and held a great feast.
 From that feast is said to descend the Silvercandle Carnival as it is known today.
desc2:
Ⅶ. The Proclamation of Vengeance
 
 Dis Galea returned into the snowbound wilderness.
 
 Words forsook him; darkness veiled his sight without end.
 
 In silence he recalled his brother's face.
 
 Had he yet trod the sacred halls of Elysium,
 
 He would have cried aloud the names of the Great Nine,
 
 Entreating the power that guides the fallen home.
 
 But blind faith was long renounced, the idols cast down,
 
 And death itself bore witness: the gods were gone.
 
 So the host kept silence, and with Dis Galea they mourned wordlessly.
 
 The soldiers, wrath bound in silence, awaited his command.
 
 The frozen earth trembled beneath his wrath.
 
 Three days and three nights his silence endured.
 
 The host waited, and waited still — for their lord to call forth vengeance, to cast the demons into dust.
 
 At last he spoke, slow and measured: "Leave these snows. Let us bide our time.
 
 The Charon are indeed our foes; yet more loathsome still is our own frailty.
 
 The demons bear no Solarian virtue. They wield their strength in wanton excess.
 
 Then must we forge a strength redoubled, to cast them down and bind them fast in chains.
 
 Better to gather strength, to lie low in wait for a just vengeance,
 
 Than to squander rage to our common ruin."

name: Silvercandle Hymn (Ⅷ)
desc:
A hymn sung at the Silvercandle Carnival, recounting its legendary origin: Soranus, younger brother to Dis Ⅰ, first emperor of Hyperborea, was struck down by the Charon. Yet after conquest was won, Dis Ⅰ chose not vengeance but peace, and held a great feast.
 From that feast is said to descend the Silvercandle Carnival as it is known today.
desc2:
Ⅷ. The Iron Hooves in Their Charge
 
 The host stirred and swelled like waters brought to the boil.
 
 Far-sighted was Dis Galea,
 
 Prudent was Dis Galea!
 
 And so they mourned with Dis Galea for Solanus,
 
 For Solanus, revered and feared, had fallen.
 
 Dirges rose and tears fell,
 
 As though a thousand stars descended all at once.
 
 The night lay veiled in mist; no guiding star remained.
 
 This day we endure the bitterness of deceit;
 
 Yet when the tide of the Great Migration next sweeps the snowbound plain:
 
 Though death descends as equal fate on every soul, Sola and Charon alike,
 
 The demons' blood shall drench the earth.
 
 Their bones shall be wrought into goblets;
 
 Their houses shall become graveyards;
 
 Their horns shall be broken and cast into Lamenting Lake, until its waters brim with ruin.
 
 And this land, bright with Phoxene, shall rise as offering unto Soranus.
 
 Thus, feeding on hatred,
 
 Dis Galea and his host endured the winter.
 
 They unsheathed their swords and seized the hamlets;
 
 They tightened their reins and trampled the houses.
 
 Yet endless massacre slowly dulled their wrath,
 
 And the Solarian, guided by reason, turned from the path of carnage and blood, 
 
 And sought instead a road of concord.

name: Silvercandle Hymn (Ⅸ)
desc:
A hymn sung at the Silvercandle Carnival, recounting its legendary origin: Soranus, younger brother to Dis Ⅰ, first emperor of Hyperborea, was struck down by the Charon. Yet after conquest was won, Dis Ⅰ chose not vengeance but peace, and held a great feast.
 From that feast is said to descend the Silvercandle Carnival as it is known today.
desc2:
Ⅸ. The Dissolving of Hatred
 
 Ten times did the ice of Lamenting Lake melt, and ten times it froze anew.
 
 And in the villages the Charon's dread deepened day by day —
 
 For ten years past it was they who had plotted a massacre that failed,
 
 And it was they who must now taste its bitter fruit.
 
 Dis Galea, clinging to life by Fate's frail thread,
 
 Endured the harsh winters of the North by means unknown,
 
 And with the silver tide of his host he laid waste to every land round about.
 
 At last he came,
 
 And with his coming an ending surely fell.
 
 With his host he cast down in swift might the fortress reared upon Soranus's grave.
 
 The Charon, in despair, murmured prayers to Mother Embla,
 
 Believing that this day would see them sink into the Misty Sea's embrace.
 
 Yet what came was neither slaughter nor conquest,
 
 But leniency beyond all measure.
 
 Dis Galea cursed Fate,
 
 Yet ten years of war had bent his heart toward peace.
 
 In his letters he wrote thus, grave and rational:
 
 "Vengeance is scarlet, fair to behold — yet it only ends in withering.
 
 Peace is silver, grievous to bear — yet it composes the song of prosperity.
 
 Even if we let the Charon's blood sink into the stone, yet the stone shall one day crumble to desert.
 
 But once the seeds of peace are sown, for centuries, for millennia, flowers shall bloom."
 
 "My Solarian brothers, burdened with hatred — let us together cast scorn upon Fate.
 
 To deny anger its dominion over the mind — that is the very proof of our humanity.
 
 These Charon, once branded Children of the Demon, 
 
 Are righteous folk who rose against the Church.
 
 Rather than cross swords and raise the dirge,
 
 Let Soranus be the first and last sacrifice.
 
 And the Charon shall mourn him with us as sisters and brothers.
 
 So long as Lamenting Lake endures,
 
 So long as the mountains stand,
 
 The name of Soranus shall be sung without end, echoing between mountain and lake.

name: Silvercandle Hymn (Ⅹ)
desc:
A hymn sung at the Silvercandle Carnival, recounting its legendary origin: Soranus, younger brother to Dis Ⅰ, first emperor of Hyperborea, was struck down by the Charon. Yet after conquest was won, Dis Ⅰ chose not vengeance but peace, and held a great feast.
 From that feast is said to descend the Silvercandle Carnival as it is known today.
desc2:
Ⅹ. Silver Candles Aflame, the Carnival Begins
 
 Thus did Galea's soldiers, the Solarian host who had reached the uttermost North,
 
 Lay down their swords, set aside their hatred,
 
 And lifted silver candles on high with hearts of mercy.
 
 Following close upon Galea, they came unto the dwellings of the Charon.
 
 White mountains stretched, the keen winds howled,
 
 And the Charon, who thought the flame of war was at hand, beheld instead from afar the silver candlelight.
 
 They marvelled: the Solarian host comes not for vengeance, but for peace!
 
 Dis I had lost a brother;
 
 Yet were not the Charon themselves a vaster host of brethren?
 
 Then the Charon brought forth their finest wine,
 
 With meats newly cured and berries preserved.
 
 They pledged kinship with Dis I,
 
 And hailed the gracious, gentle Galea as their lord.
 
 They raised a city meant to endure — 
 
 Walls, a great plaza, lofty halls, and a theatre of song.
 
 There, Solarian and Charon alike
 
 Would share their finest days without divide.
 
 All who heard Dis I proclaim that vision were enthralled;
 
 And each vowed to be the cornerstone of the Empire's enduring dream.
 
 From that day, with each returning year, 
 
 In Icelake — where Soranus fell and the tragedy found its end — 
 
 The people gather.
 
 They kindle candles in silver candlesticks,
 
 And strike the festival's first note in the Far North.
 
 The flames soar, recalling ages past;
 
 The bells resound long, and grief is cast away.
 
 So hear — hear the songs that shall never fade;
 
 Sing — sing the hymn to the everlasting Empire.

name: Boycott the Silvercandle Carnival!
desc: A hand-scrawled flyer, its jagged script so fierce you can almost hear it shouting. Line by line it denounces the Silvercandle Hymn, proclaiming the truth turned on its head.
desc2:
Charon brothers, Charon sisters — remember that verse they drilled into us when we were kids?
"Have you heard of such a carnival, where blasphemers clasp the hands of Demon's Children?"
Yeah, that one. The Silvercandle Hymn. We've heard it so many times our ears grew numb.
Every year, when that day comes, we Charon — scraping through bitter lives — stitch together masks and costumes. Because only then do the Solarian pretend to treat us as human. Only then do they hold back their scorn. They dance, they laugh — and they blast that cursed Hymn at us a hundred times over.
And I know many of you can recite its lines, maybe even feel sorry for the "kind-hearted" Dis I and his brother Soranus. Some even believe — because our ancestors supposedly killed Soranus — that we're bound to serve the Solarian forever. They say it's our destiny. To repay a blood debt. I say that's all lies.
Don't buy it.
Don't buy it!
Don't buy it!!!
The Silvercandle Carnival is a lie from start to finish. There never was a carnival. Only a massacre. And Soranus? He wasn't some poor victim. He was the butcher — the worst of them all!
 
Listen, I'll tell you another story. The truth.
