name: Shouxing Squid
desc: A small squid named after Shouxing, the god of longevity in Huaxu myth. Though diminutive, its tentacles allow it to spring through the air with startling force. In Huaxu, it is a cherished symbol of long life — on elders' birthdays, desserts shaped in its likeness are a must-have at the celebration.
desc2:
Legends speak of an immortal Wishen said to predate memory itself. Over countless ages, the weight of unforgotten thoughts swelled its head, round and heavy. At last, unable to bear the burden, it cried out to the Argent Dragon for aid. The celestial dragon answered by casting its memories into the sea. Steeped in seawater, those fragments became squids with large, swollen heads. And as the memories dissolved, the Wuyousheng's form grew ever fainter... until, at last, it was reborn as a child — unburdened, unbound, ready to begin anew.

— Qiu Ci, folklorist from Huaxu, Tales of the Grain

name: Thornbearer
desc: Covered in fine barbs, this fish puffs into a spiny sphere when threatened, inflating itself with air or water. Despite being dangerously toxic and notoriously difficult to prepare, it remains a sought-after delicacy in Huaxu.
desc2:
Death by improperly prepared Thornbearer — a classic modus operandi in Huaxu detective fiction. And in stories like these, the sleuth often delivers this line with icy resolve: "Though the Nine Chapters of Dafeng name no law for your kind, justice shall still be done!"

— Rovetta, travel writer, Rovetta in Huaxu

name: Pouchcarp
desc: A brightly coloured fish native to Huaxu, known for its pouch-like belly and bottom-dwelling habits. Though modest in size, it's prized for its tender, boneless meat — a favourite at many local restaurants.
desc2:
Each year, the Pouchcarp is among the offerings prepared for the Argent Dragon. Restaurants across Huaxu compete fiercely for the honour — in what has become the famed "Pouchcarp Cook-Off," a culinary contest where chefs showcase their skills through this beloved local fish. The winner, chosen by popular vote, earns the honour of preparing dishes for the Argent Dragon's feast.

— Rovetta, travel writer, Rovetta in Huaxu

name: Waterwyrm
desc:
A rare Huaxu fish that can grow up to four metres long. With a pointed snout and four pairs of ventral fins, it bears symmetrical markings and shimmering scales reminiscent of the Argent Dragon.
Though not protected under the Nine Chapters of Dafeng, the Waterwyrm is rarely hunted. Its likeness to the Argent Dragon stirs reverence across Huaxu — and few would risk sacrilege by putting it on a dinner table.
desc2:
First toast to the Lord of the Sea — Calm the waves, and bring us all home safe.
Second toast to the Lord of the Sea — Fill our nets with fish, shrimp, and clam.
Third toast to the Lord of the Sea — Grant fair winds and fruitful harvests across the land.
Fourth toast to the Lord of the Sea — May fortune, health, and long life be ever yours!

— Sea Blessing Chant of Huaxu Fishermen

name: Mousetail
desc: A whiskered, long-tailed fish that favours cracks and corners, and is hardy enough to thrive even in stagnant or polluted waters. Unlike real rats, it doesn't gnaw on clothing or steal food — which is why children in the slums often keep them as low-maintenance pets.
desc2:
The Mousling Fish often serves as a convenient snack for larger predators, leaving it extremely timid. Even the faintest disturbance sends it scurrying into the nearest corner. If you plan to keep a few, be sure to provide plenty of hiding spots in your aquarium.

— Harriet, nature writer, World Beneath the Waves

name: Bonegnaw Eel
desc: A smooth-skinned, scaleless creature with a tubular mouth lined with rows of sharp teeth — no upper or lower jaw. It burrows in sewer sludge and latches onto anything that gets too close... and once it does, it never lets go. Among sewer workers, it's considered the nastiest creature you can run into down there.
desc2:
"This time, the manager finally approved my sick leave. I showed up with the Bonegnaw Eel still clamped on my arm — thing was thrashing so hard, it slapped a whole splash of sewer muck right in his face."

— Yoan, sewer cleaner

name: Waterskull
desc: A fully transparent fish with fine, delicate bones. Nearly impossible to spot with the naked eye, its flesh is gelatinous and inedible — though researchers believe it may be refined into a rare, highly specialised gel.
desc2:
"This material exhibits remarkable elasticity and water resistance. In time, it may allow for the creation of instruments capable of functioning at great depths — perhaps even those that could reach the Heaventree's buried roots. And with them, we may yet trace the origins of the world."

— Emerald, Materials Researcher at the Aeolipile, Principles and Instructions for Use of New Materials

name: Screechbeast
desc: A bizarre, limbed fish that lurks in the mud and occasionally emits blood-curdling cries. Its resemblance to the Filthoid is uncanny — though whether this is mere coincidence or something more remains unknown.
desc2:
"Ee—ya! Ee-ya—ha! Ha→ha→ha↓ha↑"

— An attempt by local residents to mimic the eerie laughter echoing through the sewers

name: Aquaroach
desc: A brownish fish with six twitching fins along its sides. Its jerky movements ripple through the water — unsettling to watch, but alarmingly fast. Two antenna-like feelers jut from its head, often the first sign it's lurking nearby. Ruthless and persistent, it's even been known to pursue prey onto dry land.
desc2:
Never, ever — ever — go head-to-head with it. Where your eyes can't reach, its kin are already watching from the dark...

— A widely repeated warning

name: Stonemill Tonguefish
desc: A fish species native to Huaxu, notable for its unusual appearance: a rounded stonemill-like shape, with both eyes sitting on one side of the body. Early records claim it must merge with a perfect mirror-twin in order to swim — a tale local fishermen dismiss outright as fiction.
desc2:
In the East dwells the flounder; without its counterpart it does not swim, and thus it earns its name. In the South lies the joined-wing bird; without its mate it does not rise, and hence it is so called.
 
 — from Erya: On Lands, a Huaxu classic

name: Orchid Crab
desc: A pretty little sea crab named for the way its paddling legs fan out like orchid petals. It is common in the waters of Huaxu and delicious simply blanched. Known to nip many a curious finger — both lovable and infuriating, and all the more memorable for it.
desc2:
I've always felt that the people of Huaxu cook in two completely opposite ways: either they pile on ingredient after ingredient, like ornamenting a melody with endless grace notes, or they chase the food's original flavour with almost stubborn devotion.
 The first is best shown by a cabbage broth built on the essence of many ingredients; the second by chicken still showing blood at the bone, and Orchid Crabs simply boiled and served with a signature dipping sauce.
 
— Wym, food journalist from Luca, A Taste of Atlasia

name: Starfish
desc:
A perfectly standard starfish.
 Decent enough as decoration, though nowhere near as pretty as a pearl.
 Passable as food, but there's not much to it, so few people bother.
 As a catch, it's better than nothing, but nothing to boast about.
 In short, it's a starfish — nothing more to say, really.
desc2:
"What do you mean I came back skunked!? I caught a starfish, didn't I? That counts as a catch! How is that the same as going home empty-handed!?"
 
— an indignant angler

name: Firecracker Shrimp
desc: A vivid scarlet creature from the sea, shrimp-like in form but distinct from true shrimp, and about the length of a firecracker. Feisty by nature, it flares up at the smallest provocation, which is how it got its name. It is usually deep-fried, then stir-fried with a spiced salt and pepper mix for a fragrant, mouth-watering finish. Best enjoyed in the first month of the lunar year, shared with family as firecrackers crackle outside — spot on!
desc2:
"Ma and Pa's trust in me just collapsed. Just now."
 
"What did you do?"
 
"They left me alone in a room full of New Year's dishes — pepper-salt firecrackers, fried meatballs, cured venison, fish jelly..."
 
"Sounds delicious."
 
 Exactly. So when they woke up at midnight, the pepper-salt firecrackers were nothing but shells."
 
"...That's why you got kicked over here. I see. They didn't stuff a real firecracker in your mouth — that's love, honestly."
 
— a New Year's conversation between two brothers

name: Azurewave Kun
desc: A fierce, blue-green giant of a fish, named for how it evokes the ancient Huaxu tales of the Kun — the legendary great fish said to devour all things. Among Huaxu's fishers, having one's thigh pierced by a fast-charging Azurewave Kun is considered one of the nastiest curses you can throw at someone.
desc2:
"In the Northern Ocean dwells a fish named Kun..."
 
"Teacher... is this Kun the same as the Azurewave Kun in the sea?"
 
"No. The name is only borrowed from the classic; the Kun it speaks of isn't real."
 
"But the Azurewave Kun is also a Kun, isn't it? Why would you say it's not real?"
 
— The opening to the philosophical debate known as The Paradox of the Non-Kun Kun

name: Edgefin
desc: A river fish famed for its delicate flavour, shaped much like a small blade. Legend tells of an assassin who once hid a dagger among a dish of plain-boiled edgefin, drawing it only when his unsuspecting foe was lost in the delight of the coming meal. The tale, at least, proves two things: edgefin really do resemble blades — and they taste exceptionally good.
desc2:
"I really miss edgefin wontons... When Mother was still here, she would make them for Fushu and me every spring. But after she became… I tried to make her recipe myself after that, but I could never get it right. I wish I'd learned all her tricks back then."
 
— from Fufeng's notes

name: Bloom Perch
desc: A fierce-tempered river fish that favours live prey, so aggressive it can be landed even on an unbaited hook. At its plumpest when peach blossoms fill the spring air, it is traditionally scored and steamed, then topped with light soy sauce and hot oil — the most elaborate way Huaxu households receive honoured guests.
desc2:
Peachbloom drifts, spring rains dye the river rouge haze.
A child's oar parts the stream, fish trace its wake.
Splashes seep through dreams, rousing the silver-haired.
Before the plump perch, he forgets, for a heartbeat, the weight of his years.
 
— Anonymous, Fishing Amidst Peach Blossoms

A child's oar parts the stream, fish trace its wake.
Splashes seep through dreams, rousing the silver-haired.
Before the plump perch, he forgets, for a heartbeat, the weight of his years.
 
— Anonymous, Fishing Amidst Peach Blossoms

name: Roughskin Sculpin
desc: A long-prized food fish, though scarce in supply. Its most renowned preparation is a rich fish stew. With the first autumn breeze, Starweavers far from home inevitably long for its taste.
desc2:
"It isn't the season for Roughskin Sculpin, so obtaining this one wasn't easy — you've done well. Our guest today has come all the way from Hyperborea and will be of great help to me in the days ahead. Naturally, proper courtesies must be observed."
 
— Zhiliu, Proprietress of EverSpring

name: Phoenix Cichlid
desc: An ornamental species with a saddle-shaped dorsal fin. Juveniles are pale grey, while adults develop a range of vivid colours. Unfussy about water conditions and easy to keep.
desc2:
"Legend tells that Yang hunted across Huaxu and brought down twenty-one dread beasts. One was a giant bird in iridescent plumage, circling ever high above and impossible to strike. So Yang commanded the smiths to forge the Gale-Bolt and gave his trusted retainer Shan a great bow. Shan loosed nine arrows, each finding its mark. When the bird fell, its feathers drifted down — those that touched the earth became phoenix flowers, and those that fell upon water turned into the bright Phoenix Cichlid."
 
 — Qiu Ci, folklorist from Huaxu, Tales of the Grain

name: Emperorfish
desc: The largest freshwater fish in Huaxu, fully golden and exceedingly rare. Long taken as a symbol of emperors — though with no emperors left in Huaxu, the word now brings this giant fish to mind far sooner than any ruler of ages past.
desc2:
"The recommended procedure for landing an Emperorfish is to gather as many people as possible — ideally three hundred. Twenty should help you haul it ashore; another twenty should keep it wet while recording its length; a further twenty should see to pushing it safely back into the river. As for the remaining two hundred and forty, they're simply there to prove you're not making the whole thing up.
Truth be told, I've never caught one myself — but if I ever do, I'll follow these steps to the letter."
 
— The Angler's Guide of Huaxu

name: Ink Glancer
desc: A slender, brightly coloured bottom-dweller that excels at ambush. Its large eyes glow softly at night, likely to lure unwary small fish close. To a fisherman peering into the dark water, they can look like pairs of blue-glowing eyes lurking on the riverbed.
desc2:
"They took a small boat and rowed into an underground cavern. They had already crossed countless dangers in search of the relics left by a famed general serving under Dafeng, their blades worn to the bone. In the total darkness, everyone was on edge — until a scream tore through the silence. Something glowing rose from the black water: a ghostly face with two blue-green lights staring straight at them."

— Huaxu adventure novel, The Twelve Tombs

name: Mudleaper
desc: A small fish often seen in pairs, nimble enough to leap and able to crawl briefly on land. It lives across coastal shallows and riverbanks, digging small dens and keeping its partner wet by splashing water over it. This behaviour made it a symbol of mutual devotion in old texts, and in recent years its quirky appearance has made it rather popular.
desc2:
Cutting wheat and planting again,

gardenias bloom and magnolias then.

Butterflies drift and bees come humming,

mudlarks skim where the reeds are softly swaying.

See the mandarin ducks drift side by side,

and I wonder what my young man is thinking.

— Huaxu folk song, Night Song of the Mudlark

name: Blindlight
desc: A fish that dwells in lightless environments. Its body is milky, pale, and translucent with a pearly sheen, and its eyes have completely degenerated. As rare as hen's teeth.
desc2:
"The Blindlight surrendered its eyes to a life of darkness — just as the people of Huaxu once laid down their weapons to live in harmony. We, too, could remain content like that... but only if our surroundings never changed, and nothing from beyond ever reached us."
 
— Lin Caocao, biologist from Huaxu

name: Toad
desc: A species that inhabits dark, damp places, with extremely rough skin and a back that changes colour with the seasons. It is long valued as a traditional medicinal ingredient  — though many find its appearance decidedly unattractive.
desc2:
"...I honestly cannot imagine what led Fufeng to study this as a medicinal material."

— Fushu, physician from Huaxu

name: Flutterfin
desc: A denizen of the dim and dank, with large pectoral fins tipped with spines. Its bright coloration and swimming motion give it a moth-like appearance. Highly poisonous, its fins were once fashioned into weapons during the ancient era.
desc2:
"Hah! This is the best gift I've ever received! Heh-heh... One of these days you're going to swing a blade I forged myself — its edge smeared thick with poison. Oh — and when that day comes, do try not to lick it to play cool."

— Lunosmith

name: Star-Spotted Sculpin
desc: A species found in the brackish waters where Huaxu's rivers meet the sea. Its flanks are mottled with pale, star-like markings that shimmer faintly in low light. When hooked after dusk, its scales catch the light with a star-like sheen, as though a fragment of a constellation has been lifted from the water.
desc2:
Huaxu is home to a well-known tale: Monkeys Scooping the Moon. Yet it may not have been the moon the monkeys reached for, but a patch of starlight scattered across the pond's surface.

— Huaxu journal, Classical Tales Revisited

name: Venomspine Catfish
desc: A small marine catfish that can pass for an eel at first glance, until the barbels at its mouth give it away. Aggressive and quick to pick fights despite its size, it's also highly social, gathering in schools that spend much of the day jostling and jabbing at one another with their hardened, venomous barbs.
desc2:
When the people of Huaxu first told me they were preparing a Venomspine Catfish feast for me, I flat-out refused. For a moment, I wondered whether I'd slighted Huaxu cuisine in one of my pieces, and they meant to poison me with the fish. As it turned out, I was entirely mistaken. Silky-smooth, with a faint tingle on the tongue — I assumed they'd used peppercorns, only to learn it came from the venom itself. How do the Huaxu manage to make something poisonous taste this good!?

— Wym, food journalist from Luca, A Taste of Atlasia

name: Prismatic Seahorse
desc: A seahorse variety whose body resembles a raw gemstone. It is prized for display and medicinal use rather than for consumption.
desc2:
"Good grief... I've been fishing all my life, and I still can't tell if this Prismatic Seahorse even counts as a fish."

— An old fisherman, deep in thought

name: Jade Sprat
desc: A slender marine fish found along Huaxu's coast. Soft-fleshed and nutrient-rich, it is commonly used as bait or as feed for larger fish. Its melancholy gaze makes it look as if it already knows how its story ends.
desc2:
"Jade Sprat in my mouth, booze in my gut — I strut this shore like I own the lot!"

— A drunken Huaxu local, sprawled on the sand, shooing gulls from his fried fish

name: Dawnscale
desc: Found along Huaxu's coast, most often in deeper waters. Despite living in the depths, the Dawnscale gleams with a bright, uniform golden sheen, as though a sliver of dawn has been caught beneath the sea. Smaller specimens fetch little, but prices climb steeply with size, earning it the local nickname "gold in the water".
desc2:
"Look! A whole patch of gold out there — we're gonna be rich! Hahahaha... Huh? What do you mean it's darting and leaping?"

— An overexcited foreign sailor

name: Haojing Mitten Crab
desc: One of the best-known crabs from the waters of Haojing, prized for its size and rich flavour. It's also high in protein and minerals. Best enjoyed when the autumn winds set in: steamed, then dipped in vinegar with thin shreds of ginger. A seasonal favourite across Huaxu.
desc2:
"'Course it's pricey! Real Haojing Mitten Crab, this. Don't be asking where it was raised or where I hauled it up— long as it's had a little swim in Haojing's waters, it counts as the real thing."

— A fishmonger at Haze Market, calling out to passers-by

name: Croaker Carp
desc: A small wild freshwater fish found in abundance across Huaxu, remarkably hardy and highly adaptable. Its flesh is delicate but riddled with fine bones, making it better suited to soups and broths than to frying or grilling. When it surfaces to gulp air, it often lets out a frog-like croak, hence its name.
desc2:
"Well, I'll be — turns out this plain little Croaker Carp is the ancestor of quite a few ornamental breeds."

— An unnamed scholar, picking fish bones from between his teeth while leafing through a compendium of Huaxu anecdotes

name: Lotusleaf
desc: A curious fish that bears a lotus-leaf-like growth atop its head, making it exceptionally hard to spot among floating leaves. Even veteran fishermen struggle to tell, at a glance, which leaves are real and which are Lotusleaf in disguise.
desc2:
"Not sure why, but just looking at it makes everything feel... peaceful. Even a fish this tiny still gets its own little leaf to shelter under.

What? You're telling me that isn't a real leaf — it's the fish's own camouflage? ...So even fish don't get peace for free? They have to grow it just to survive!?"

— A burnt-out thirty-something office drone

name: Bronze Drum
desc: Native to Huaxu, its scales gleam like polished bronze. In ancient times, its scales were once used as currency. Some members of the Jishu Sect see it as an auspicious omen and make offerings in its honour.
desc2:
The Bronze Drum takes its name from its resemblance to ancient bronze vessels. Once cooked, its scales take on a faint reddish glow that whets the appetite. Drizzle hot oil over it just before serving, and the flesh turns firm and springy — utterly moreish.

— Wym, food journalist from Luca, A Taste of Atlasia

name: Crimson Crest
desc: One of Huaxu's prized freshwater species, distinguished by its vivid red crest and aggressive temperament. When hunting, it doesn't strike immediately. Instead, it circles its prey until it becomes disoriented, then delivers a single decisive bite. In bearing, it resembles a swaggering general wearing a crimson helm.

name: Stinker
desc: A rare scavenger fish whose diet leaves it with a lingering stench that no amount of cleaning can fully remove. In Huaxu, it's widely regarded as one of the worst-tasting fish ever to reach the table.
desc2:
"Yuck! What is this — some kind of torture device? How's eating this any different from chewing on manure?"

— Wym, food journalist from Luca

name: Taroheart Clam
desc: A clam found in turbid waters, its shell often caked in silt and grime. Yet beneath the muck lies tender pink flesh that becomes unexpectedly sweet and aromatic when cooked — hence the name.
desc2:
"Freshly dredged Taroheart Clams! Bit of mud's only natural. Don't you worry — old family trade, this. No way I'm ruining my name by slapping mud on any old shell and calling it 'Taroheart'!"

— A fishmonger calling out in a Haojing market

name: Riverworm
desc: A wormlike invertebrate resembling an earthworm, typically found in dark, stagnant waters. It is unusually plump and almost the colour of raw flesh. It is valued for its medicinal properties and prized by fishermen as bait.
desc2:
"I only meant to use up the bait and head home. Next thing I know, I reel in a Riverworm. Figured I might as well use it as bait. Then I caught another. So I used that one. Caught another. ...And now look at the time."

— A middle-aged fisherman, explaining his late return to his wife

name: Lanterneye
desc: A small fish inhabiting lightless waters, notable for its disproportionately large, luminous eyes. Even in turbid currents heavy with silt and sediment, their glow cuts through the murk.
desc2:
"They call it Lanterneye. At first I thought that was a bit generous — more like two bulbs stuck on a sorry excuse for a fish. But look at it long enough... and you start to see the charm."

— A fisherman, deep in thought

name: Siltshark
desc: A freshwater predator native to Huaxu's turbid waters. It buries itself in the silt and lies in wait for prey to draw near, then bursts from the mud and strikes in a single explosive motion. In parts of Huaxu, it ranks among the region's apex predators.
desc2:
"Good grief... I've been fishing all my life and never once questioned it. Turns out the Siltshark isn't a shark at all. Reckon 'Siltshark' sounds a fair bit better than 'mudfish' when you're bragging about your catch. No wonder it stuck."

— An old fisherman, deep in thought

name: Training Rod
desc: A fishing rod crafted by Lunosmith, featuring a surface monitor styled after Cinder, her trusty little assistant. When a fish bites, Cinder lights up to signal it — though according to customer feedback, some folks got so mesmerised watching it glow, they ended up going home with an empty bucket.
desc2:
A thousand casts a day — that's just the basics for any beginner. And by the time you're done, even if you've caught no fish, you'll at least have the arm of a decent swordsman.

— A veteran angler who prefers to stay anonymous

name: Beginner's Rod
desc: A fishing rod crafted by Lunosmith, featuring a surface monitor styled after Cinder, her trusty little assistant. When a fish bites, Cinder lights up to signal it — though according to customer feedback, some folks got so mesmerised watching it glow, they ended up going home with an empty bucket.
desc2:
Remember: even a cooked duck might fly off — so how much easier for a live fish to escape? Until it's flopping in your basket, down to the last second, the last breath... it's not truly yours.

— A veteran angler with a rueful smile

name: Advanced Rod
desc: A fishing rod crafted by Lunosmith, featuring a surface monitor styled after Cinder, her trusty little assistant. When a fish bites, Cinder lights up to signal it — though according to customer feedback, some folks got so mesmerised watching it glow, they ended up going home with an empty bucket.
desc2:
Fish I desire, and bear paws I desire too. But if both can't be had — well, if no fish will bite, I'll take the paws.

— A veteran angler sharpening his knife

name: Expert Rod
desc: A fishing rod crafted by Lunosmith, featuring a surface monitor styled after Cinder, her trusty little assistant. When a fish bites, Cinder lights up to signal it — though according to customer feedback, some folks got so mesmerised watching it glow, they ended up going home with an empty bucket.
desc2:
I remember — it was just past midnight. A Lamenting Lake Trout had taken the bait. Couldn't see a thing, but I knew it had to weigh at least eight kilos. Too bad my rod snapped clean in half through the fight! But hey... that's fishing. It's not about the catch — it's a kind of spiritual practice. A test of patience. The result doesn't matter. Honestly, I'd forgotten all about that night... until you brought it up. Anyway — check out this new rod! Solid as a rock. Unless it's the Lake Monster itself, nothing's breaking this one. Hehe...

— A teary-eyed veteran angler

name: Grandmaster Rod
desc: A fishing rod crafted by Lunosmith, featuring a surface monitor styled after Cinder, her trusty little assistant. When a fish bites, Cinder lights up to signal it — though according to customer feedback, some folks got so mesmerised watching it glow, they ended up going home with an empty bucket.
desc2:
"Whoa! Got one! I caught a fish! Haha!"
"Are you blind!? That fish's on my hook! Get your line off my Limited Edition, Cinder-Certified, Iridescent Master Rod — right now!"

— A veteran angler (briefly joyful), and his unlucky friend

name: Artificer Rod: Rust Red
desc:
Huaxu legends tell of a master angler whose true name has long been forgotten. People simply call him Old Angler Jiang. They say he could cast an empty line and still land a fish, every time.
Everyone knows tricks like that are wishful thinking — but commissioning a Jishu artisan to recreate his rod is easy enough.
desc2:
Artificer Rod? What a rip-off! You hook the little ones with bait, then use them to land the big ones — that's how it works! Can't believe I've wasted an entire afternoon on this.
— A Huaxu angler, seething

name: Artificer Rod: Violet
desc:
Huaxu legends tell of a master angler whose true name has long been forgotten. People simply call him Old Angler Jiang. They say he could cast an empty line and still land a fish, every time.
Everyone knows tricks like that are wishful thinking — but commissioning a Jishu artisan to recreate his rod is easy enough.
desc2:
This rod really does have something to it. I'd only just taken it out, and people were already crowding in to lecture me — saying Artificer Rods are useless, that it's all superstition, and so on.
— A Huaxu would-be angler, intrigued

name: Basic Lure
desc: A standard lure meant to attract a fish's attention — whether it actually helps you catch anything... is another matter entirely.
desc2:
A true master angler needs only one rod, one bucket, and a deft hand.

— A veteran angler with an empty creel and not a crumb of bait left

name: Wiggling Lure
desc: A special lure that shortens bite time. Maybe it's the way it wriggles — irresistible to most underwater dwellers.
desc2:
Plenty of anglers raise their own bait. It's economical, convenient, and efficient. Just... make sure the lid on your bait box is tight. I mean really tight.

— A veteran angler buying insecticide

name: Like Attracts Like
desc: A formulated bait that boosts your odds of luring fish variants. To a creature with eccentric tastes, maybe a glinting hunk of scrap can pass for fine cuisine.
desc2:
Variants are fish that went a little... sideways. No telling what they'll bite. Honestly, I'm starting to think they remember more than three seconds — it's the only way to explain why they keep circling that same scrap of metal every time I toss it in.

— A veteran angler suspiciously favoured by variants

name: Cluckin' Good
desc: A deceptively plain-looking lure, crafted from top-grade ingredients. Even the pickiest of fish keep pecking until the very last crumb is gone.
desc2:
"Run! It's the Master of Chumming!"

— A veteran angler, fleeing for dear life

name: EverSpring Voucher
desc: A trade voucher issued by EverSpring, Zhiliu's guild.

name: Wonder Box
desc:
Transform!
Can be equipped and used in your Tactical Backpack

name: Redscale
desc: Silver scale, jade scale, red scale... dead scale. Wait — what fish is this supposed to be?

name: Civil & Martial Tokens
desc:
A set of scoring tokens prepared by the Grand Incense Rite for use in the trials. Before Huaxu's prohibition on fighting, competitions were divided into civil and martial categories, each with its own tokens for tallying points. Though martial force was later forbidden throughout the realm, the scoring system endured; only the distinction between Civil and Martial Tokens was set aside.
 
 Now, under the new format, Martial Tokens have been reinstated. A competitor's final score is calculated from the combined total of Civil and Martial Tokens.

name: Invitation
desc: Since its launch, the Incense Proving has drawn widespread attention across Huaxu, with its star contestants earning particular acclaim. To inspire more young talents amid the changes sweeping Huaxu, the organisers have invited these standout competitors to take part in an even more demanding Invitational, and issued invitations to them accordingly.

name: Sigil: Phoxhunter - Lumino
desc:
A sigil for summoning Combat Partners. It is a staff to lean on in a battle, a pact of companionship, and an oath unspoken.
Heartfelt prayers shall be answered, and the desired one shall appear by your side.
desc2:
"Our tale spans over two millennia: a saga of embrace and massacre, of furore and mercy. History ebbs and flows like the celestial dance of the sun and the moon – constant and cyclical. In the grand tapestry of time recounted in these pages, I am but a mere observer, as insignificant as a flake of Hyperborean snow, a leaf from Aethyrie, a drop in Luca's waters, or a grain from Khemet's sands. Yet, in this immense cosmos, I harbour the hope that snowflakes will forge snowfields, leaves will form forests, drops of water will coalesce into rivers, and grains will gather to sculpt deserts. As all singular entities unite, history shall pivot in our favour."

— Betwixt Leaves And Branches — History of Atlasia, by Comnena, Chief Librarian of the Aethyrie Cloud Cavern Library
